et $x = u$ for part (1) and $x = b$ for part (2). Let $\mathscr{X} = \mathscr{X}_{{\mathbf m}} = \{{\mathbf n}: {\mathbf n}$ is bounded if $x = b;$ and $({\mathbf m} {\restriction} M_{{\mathbf m}}) \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf n}$ and $L_{{\mathbf n}} \setminus M_{{\mathbf m}} = t / E_{{\mathbf n}}''$ for some $t,$ hence $\Vert L_{{\mathbf n}} \Vert \leq \lambda_{2}\}.$

    We define a two-place relation ${\mathscr E}$ on ${\mathscr X}$:

    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_0$]  $\mathbf n_1 {\mathscr E} \mathbf n_2$ {\underline{iff}} \, $(\mathbf n_1,\mathbf n_2 \in {\mathscr X}$ and) there is an isomorphism $h$ from $\mathbf n_1$ onto $\mathbf n_2$ over $\mathbf m {\restriction} M_{\mathbf m}$, 
        that is: an isomorphism from $L_{\mathbf n_1}$  onto $L_{\mathbf n_2}$ over $M_{\mathbf m}$ (as partial orders) such that: 
        
        \begin{enumerate} 
            \item[(a)] $t \in L_{\mathbf n_1} \Rightarrow u_{\mathbf n_2,h(t)} = \{h(s):s  \in u_{\mathbf n_1,t}\}$, 
            
            \item[(b)] $t \in L_{\mathbf n_1} \Rightarrow {\mathscr P}_{\mathbf n_2,h(t)} = \{\{h(s):s \in u\}:u \in {\mathscr P}_{\mathbf n_1,t}\}$, 
            
            \item[(c)] $s,t \in L_{\mathbf n_1} \Rightarrow (s E'_{\mathbf n_1 } t \Leftrightarrow h(s) E'_{\mathbf n_2 } h(t))$.   
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate} 

    Clearly ${\mathscr E}$ is an equivalence relation.
    
    By our assumptions $\chi \ge 2^{\lambda_2}$ and $\mathbf n \in {\mathscr X} \Rightarrow |L_{\mathbf n}| \le \lambda_2 \wedge (\forall t \in L_{{\mathbf n}})({\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf n}, t} \subseteq [L_{{\mathbf n}, < t}]^{\leq \lambda}),$  hence recalling $\lambda_2 = (\lambda_2)^\lambda$  clearly ${\mathscr E}$ has $\le 2^{\lambda_2}$ equivalence classes and let $\langle \mathbf n_\alpha:\alpha <
    2^{\lambda_2} \rangle$ be a set of representatives (not necessary, but no harm
    in allowing repetitions).  
    
    By \ref{c28}(2) and \ref{c31} we can find $\mathbf n$ such that:
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_1$]  $(a) \quad \mathbf m \le_{\mathbf M} \mathbf n \in \mathbf M_\chi,$
        
        \item[${{}}$]  $(b) \quad$ for every $\alpha < 2^{\lambda_2}$ we can find $\langle t_{\alpha,i}:i < \chi\rangle$ such that:
        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[${{}}$]  $(\alpha) \quad t_{\alpha,i} \in L_{\mathbf n} \backslash L_{\mathbf m},$
            
            \item[${{}}$]  $(\beta) \quad (\alpha \ne \beta) \vee (i \ne j)  \Rightarrow t_{\alpha,i}/E_{\mathbf n} \ne t_{\beta,j}/E_{\mathbf n},$
            
            \item[${{}}$]  $(\gamma) \quad \mathbf n {\restriction}  (t_{\alpha,i}/E_{\mathbf n})$ is ${\mathscr E}$-equivalent to $\mathbf n_\alpha$,
            see \ref{c5}(0) on $t_{\alpha,i}/E_{\mathbf n}$.
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}

    We shall now  prove that $\mathbf n$ is as required. Let $\mathbf n \le_{\mathbf M} \mathbf n_1 \le_{\mathbf M} \mathbf n_2, $ and $ {\mathbf n}_{1}, {\mathbf n}_{2}$ are bounded when $x = b$   and define ${\mathscr F}$ as the set of functions $f$ such that some $L_1, L_2$ satisfy:
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_2$]  $(a) \quad L_\ell \subseteq L_{\mathbf n_\ell}$,
        
        \item[${{}}$]    $(b) \quad M_ \mathbf{m} = M_ \mathbf{n} \subseteq L_1  \cap L_2$,
        
        \item[${{}}$]  $(c) \quad L_\ell$ has cardinality $\le \lambda_2$,
        
        \item[${{}}$]  $(d) \quad L_\ell$ is $E_{\mathbf n_{\ell} }$-closed, i.e.  $M_ \mathbf{m} \subseteq L_{\ell}$ and $ t
        \in L_\ell \backslash M_{\mathbf m} \Rightarrow t/E_{\mathbf n_2} \subseteq L_\ell$, 
          
        \item[${{}}$]  $(e) \quad f$ is an isomorphism from  $\mathbf n_2 {\restriction} L_1$ onto $\mathbf n_2 {\restriction} L_2$  over $M_{\mathbf m}$, i.e.:  
        
        \begin{enumerate}
        \item[${{\bullet_1}}$]  $ \quad f$ is a one-to-one mapping from $L_1$ onto $L_2$, 
        
        \item[${{\bullet _2}}$]  $\quad f {\restriction} M_{\mathbf m}$ is the identity,
        
        \item[${{\bullet _3}}$]  $ \quad f$ maps $\le_{\mathbf n_2} {\restriction} L_1$ onto $\le_{\mathbf n_2} {\restriction} L_2$, 
        
        \item[${{\bullet _4}}$] $\quad $  $ s E'_{\mathbf{n} _1}  t  \Leftrightarrow f(s) E'_{\mathbf n_2} f(t)$,
        
        
        \item[${{\bullet _5}}$] $\quad$ for $s,t \in L_1$ we have $s \in u_{\mathbf n_2,t} \Leftrightarrow f(s) \in u_{\mathbf n_2,f(t)}.$
          
        \item[$\bullet_{6}$] for $t \in L_{1}$ we have ${\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf n}_{2}, f(t)} = \{ \{ f(s): s \in u \}: u \in {\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf n}_{1}, t}, u \subseteq L_{1} \}.$ 
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}
    
    Clearly,
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_3$]  if $f \in {\mathscr F}$ and $L' \subseteq L_{\mathbf n_1}, L'' \subseteq L_{\mathbf n_2}$ and $|L'| + |L''| \le \lambda_2$ {\underline{then}} \, for some $g \in {\mathscr F}$ extending $f$ we have: 
        
        \begin{enumerate} 
            \item[(a)] $L' \subseteq {\rm dom}(g) $,
            
            \item[(b)] $ L'' \subseteq {\rm rang}(g)$,  
            
            \item[(c)] ${\rm rang}(g) \backslash (L'' \cup  {\rm rang}(f)) \subseteq L_{\mathbf n_{2}}$,
            
            \item[(d)] ${\rm dom}(g) \backslash (L'   
            \cup  {\rm dom}(f)) \subseteq L_{\mathbf n_{1}}.$
        \end{enumerate} 
    \end{enumerate}
    
    We can finish as in the parallel of the Tarski-Vaught criterion for ${\mathbb L}_{\infty,\lambda^+_2}$  but we shall elaborate.  That is, first we can prove by
    induction on the ordinal $\gamma < |L_{\mathbf n_2}|^+$ (and in fact just $\gamma < \|M_{\mathbf n_2}\|^+$) that $ (*)_4-(*)_6 $ below holds: 
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_4$]  letting $L_\gamma = L^{{\rm dp}}_{\mathbf n_2,\gamma}$, if

            \item[(b)]  $g$ induces an isomorphism $\hat g$ from  ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}({\rm dom}(g) \cap L_\gamma)$ onto ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}({\rm rang}(g) \cap L_\gamma)$, that is: $\hat

                \item[$(\gamma)$]  $g$ maps ${\rm dom}(p)$ onto ${\rm dom}(q)$ and $s \in {\rm dom}(p) \Rightarrow {\rm tr}(p(s)) = {\rm tr}(q(g(s)))$, 
                
                \item[$(\delta)$]   if $s \in {\rm dom}(g),g(s) = t \in {\rm rang}(g)$ and $\let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-

    By the choice of $ \mathbf{n} $ as very wide and full (see Definition \ref{c39}), also $\mathbf{n} \upharpoonright (\mathfrak{A} \cap L_ \mathbf{n} )$ is very wide and full of cardinality $ \chi  $. But we have  $ \mathbf{n} \upharpoonright (\mathfrak{A} \cap L_ \mathbf{n} )

Now  easily $ g $ can be extended to an automorphism of  $\mathbf{n} ^*_2 $. The promised statement now follows.]
    
    Second, 
     
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_5$]  ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L_\gamma \cap L_{\mathbf n_1})  \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L_\gamma)$.
    \end{enumerate}

    Also if $p_1,p_2 \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L_\gamma \cap L_{\mathbf n_1})$ are compatible in
    ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L_\gamma)$ let $q \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L_\gamma)$  be a common upper bound there.  We can find an $E_{\mathbf n_2}$-closed $L' \subseteq  L_{\mathbf n_1}$ of cardinality $\le \lambda_2$ (recalling $\mathbf n \in {\mathscr X} \Rightarrow |L_{\mathbf n}| \le
    \lambda_2$) such that $p_1,p_2 \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_1}(L')$ and  $E_{\mathbf n_2}$-closed $L'' \subseteq L_{{\mathbf n}_{1}}$ of cardinality $\le \lambda_2$ such that $L' \subseteq L''$ and $q \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L'')$. Now we can find $f_1 \in {\mathscr F}$ such that ${\rm dom}(f_1) = \cup\{t/E_{\mathbf n_2}:t \in L'\} \cup M_{{\mathbf m}}$ recalling that $t/E_{\mathbf m} \supseteq M_{\mathbf m}$, see \ref{c5}(0) and $f_1$ is the identity. Then by $(*)_3$ we can find $f_2 \in {\mathscr F}$ extending $f_1$ with ${\rm dom}(f_2) = \cup\{t/E_{\mathbf n_2}:t \in L''\}$ and ${\rm rang}(f_2) \backslash {\rm rang}(f_1) \subseteq L_{\mathbf n_1}$.     \models ``(p_1 \le \hat f_2(q)) \wedge (p_2 \le
    \hat f_2(q))"$ and $\hat f_2(q) \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L_\gamma \cap L_{\mathbf n_1})$ recalling
    $(*)_4$.  So $p_1,p_2$ are compatible also in ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L_\gamma \cap L_{\mathbf n_1})$.  
    Obviously, if $p_1,p_2 \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L_\gamma \cap L_{\mathbf n_1})$ are compatible in ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L_\gamma \cap L_{\mathbf n_1  }),$ say, $q$ witnesses, then
    $q$ is a common upper bound of  $p_1,p_2$ in ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2} (L_\gamma)$.
    
    So every antichain of ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L_\gamma \cap L_{\mathbf n_1})$ is an antichain of ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L_\gamma)$.  Similarly to the above every maximal
    antichain of ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L_\gamma \cap L_{\mathbf n_1})$ is a maximal antichain of ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L_\gamma)$; similarly for the
    other direction.  So we are done.]
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_6$]  ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_1}(L_\gamma \cap L_{\mathbf n_1}) = {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L_\gamma \cap L_{\mathbf n_1}) \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L_\gamma)$.
    \end{enumerate}
    
    [Why?  We prove this by induction on $\gamma$, as in proving the Tarski-Vaught criterion is sufficient (we shall  elaborate  later in the proof of \ref{e35}, more specifically $\boxplus_4$ proves a similar statement in detail with weaker assumptions).]
    
    Hence (using $\gamma = |L_{\mathbf n_2}|^+$),
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_7$]  ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_1} \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}$.
    \end{enumerate}
     
    Hence for every $L \subseteq L_{\mathbf n_1}$ by \ref{c28}(4)  we have ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_1}(L) = 
    {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}(L)$ as required for ${\mathbf n} \in {\mathbf M}_{{\rm ec}}$, see Definition \ref{c34}.

\label{c58}
    1) For ${\mathbf m} \in M,$ let ${\mathbf n} = {\mathbf m}^{[\rm{bd}]}$ be ${\mathbf m} {\restriction} L_{{\mathbf m}}^{\rm{bd}},$ where $L_{{\mathbf m}}^{{\rm bd}} = \{s \in L_{{\mathbf m}}:$ for some $t \in M_{{\mathbf m}}$ we have $s / E_{{\mathbf m}}' \subseteq L_{{\mathbf m}(\leq t)}$ or just for some ${\mathscr X} \in [M_{{\mathbf m}}]^{\leq \lambda}$ we have $s / E_{{\mathbf m}}' \subseteq \bigcup \{ L_{{\mathbf m}(\leq t)}: t \in X \} \}.$ 
    
    1A) For ${\mathbf m} \in {\mathbf M},$ let ${\mathbf n} := {\mathbf m}^{[\rm{wbd}]}$ be ${\mathbf m} {\restriction} L_{{\mathbf m}}^{\rm{wbd}},$ where $L_{{\mathbf m}}^{\rm{wbd}} := \bigcup \{ L_{{\mathbf m}(\leq t)}: t \in M_{{\mathbf m}} \}.$ 
    
    2) Assume ${\mathbf n}_{1} \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf m}_{1}, {\mathbf n}_{1} \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf n}_{2}$ and $L_{{\mathbf n}_{2}} \cap L_{{\mathbf m}_{1}} = L_{{\mathbf n}_{1}}.$ Then let ${\mathbf m}_{2} = {\mathbf n}_{2} \underset{ {\mathbf n}_{1} }\oplus {\mathbf m}_{1}$ be defined by: 
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] the set of elements of $L_{{\mathbf m}_{2}}$ is $L_{{\mathbf m}_{1}} \cup L_{{\mathbf m}_{2}},$
        
        \item[(b)] $<_{{\mathbf m}_{2}}$ is the transitive closure of $<_{{\mathbf n}_{2}} \cup <_{{\mathbf m}_{1}},$ 
        
        \item[(c)] $E_{{\mathbf m}_{2}}' = E_{{\mathbf n}_{2}}' \cup E_{{\mathbf m}_{1}}',$
            
        \item[(d)] $u_{{\mathbf m}_{2}, t}$ is: 
            
        \begin{itemize}
            \item $u_{{\mathbf m}_{2}, t}$ if $t \in L_{{\mathbf n}_{2}} \setminus L_{{\mathbf n}_{1}},$
                
            \item $u_{{\mathbf m}_{1}, t}$ if $t \in L_{{\mathbf m}_{1}} \setminus L_{{\mathbf n}_{1}},$
                
            \item $u_{{\mathbf n}_{2}} \cup u_{{\mathbf m}_{1}, t}$ if $t \in L_{{\mathbf m}_{1}}$ (so in $u_{{\mathbf n}_{1}, t}$ if $L \in L_{{\mathbf m}_{1}} \setminus M_{{\mathbf m}_{0}}$).
        \end{itemize}
            
        \item[(e)] ${\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf m}, t}$ is defined naturally, that is: 
            
        \begin{itemize}
            \item ${\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf m}_{2}, t}$ if $t \in L_{{\mathbf n}_{2}} \setminus L_{{\mathbf n}_{1}},$
                
            \item ${\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf n}_{2}, t}$ if $t \in L_{{\mathbf n}_{2}} \setminus L_{{\mathbf n}_{1}},$
                
            \item ${\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf n}_{2}} \cup {\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf m}_{1}, t}$ if $t \in L_{{\mathbf m}_{1}}$ except when $t \in M_{{\mathbf m}_{1}}^{{ \rm fat}}$ (so in ${\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf n}_{1}, t}$ if $L \in L_{{\mathbf m}_{1}} \setminus M_{{\mathbf m}_{0}}$),
                
            \item $[u_{{\mathbf m}_{2}, t}]^{\leq \lambda}$ if $t \in M_{{\mathbf m}_{1}}^{{ \rm fat}}.$
        \end{itemize}
    \end{enumerate}

\label{c61}
    1) In \ref{c58}(1) indeed ${\mathbf m}^{[{\rm bd}]} \in {\mathbf M}$ and moreover it is bounded.

\label{b5}
    Let ${\mathbb P}$ be a forcing notion and $Y \subseteq {\mathbb P}$ and $\chi$ a regular cardinal.
    
    1) Let ${\mathbb L}_\chi(Y)$ be the set of sentences formed from $\{p:p \in {\mathbb P}\}$ closing under the operations $\neg p$ and $\bigwedge\limits_{i < \alpha} p_i$, for $\alpha < \chi$; so (infinitary) propositional logic.
    
    2) For a directed  $\mathbf G \subseteq {\mathbb P}$ and $\psi \in {\mathbb L}_\chi(Y)$ we define
    the truth value $\psi[\mathbf G]$ naturally (by induction on $\psi$ starting with $p[\mathbf G] = {\rm true} \Leftrightarrow p \in \mathbf G$).
    
    3) Let ${\mathbb L}^+_\chi(Y,{\mathbb P})$, the ${\mathbb L}_\chi$-closure of $Y$ for ${\mathbb P}$, (where $Y \subseteq {\mathbb P}$; if $Y = {\mathbb P}$ we may omit $Y$) be the following partial order:
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$\bullet$]   set of elements $\{\psi \in {\mathbb L}_\chi(Y,{\mathbb P}): \, \nVdash_{{\mathbb P}} ``\psi[\let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3\mathbf G$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}] =$ false"$\},$
        
        \item[$\bullet$]  the order $\psi_1 \le \psi_2$ iff $\Vdash_{{\mathbb P}}$ ``if $\psi_2[\let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3\mathbf G$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}] =$ true then $\psi_1[\let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3\mathbf G$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}] =$ true".
    \end{enumerate}
    
    4) The completion of ${\mathbb P}$ is the ${\mathbb L}_\chi$-closure of ${\mathbb P}$ which is  ${\mathbb L}_\chi^{+}({\mathbb P})= \mathbb{L} ^+_\chi (\mathbb{P}, \mathbb{P} )$  where $\chi$ is minimal such that ${\mathbb P}$ satisfies the $\chi$-c.c.
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- claim-9: body_md -->
\label{b8}
    For a cardinal $\chi$ and forcing notion ${\mathbb P}$ and $Y \subseteq {\mathbb P}$ we have:
    
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)]  ${\mathbb L}^+_\chi(Y,{\mathbb P})$ is a forcing notion, 
        
        \item[(b)]  ${\mathbb P} \lessdot {\mathbb L}^+_\chi({\mathbb P})$ under the natural identification\footnote{Pedantically ${\mathbb P} \lessdot' {\mathbb L}^+_{\chi_{1}}[{\mathbb P}]$, see \ref{b11}(8), because ${\mathbb L}^+_\chi[{\mathbb P}] \models ``p \le q"$ {\underline{iff}} \, $q \Vdash_{{\mathbb P}} ``p \in \let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3\mathbf G$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}_{{\mathbb P}}"$.},
        
        \item[(c)]  ${\mathbb L}^+_\chi(Y,{\mathbb P}) \lessdot {\mathbb L}^+_\chi({\mathbb P})$, 
        
        \item[(d)]  ${\mathbb L}^+_{\chi_1}(Y,{\mathbb P}) \lessdot {\mathbb L}^+_{\chi_2}(Y,{\mathbb P})$ when $\chi_1 \le \chi_2$ are regular, 
        
        \item[(e)]  if ${\mathbb P}$ satisfies the $\chi_1$-c.c. and $\chi_1 < \chi_2$ are regular, {\underline{then}} \, ${\mathbb L}^+_{\chi_1}(Y,{\mathbb P})$ is essentially equal to ${\mathbb L}^+_{\chi_2}(Y,{\mathbb P})$, i.e. up to the natural equivalence of elements in a quasi order, 
        
        \item[(f)]  if $Y = {\mathbb P}$ then ${\mathbb P}$ is a dense subset of ${\mathbb L}^+_\chi({\mathbb P})$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end claim-9 -->

\label{b36}
    1) We say ${\mathbf m}$ is essentially $(< \mu)-$directed (if $\mu = \aleph_{0}$ we may omit it) \underline{when}: if $L \subseteq M, \vert L \vert < \mu$ then for some $t \in M_{{\mathbf m}},$ we have: 
    
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[$\bullet$]  $s \in L \Rightarrow s <_{{\mathbf m}} t \wedge s \in u_{t}$ so $M_{{\mathbf m}}$ is directed\footnote{Why not add $\{ s \} \in {\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf m}, t}$? See \ref{c37}(13).}). 
    \end{itemize}
    
    [Note that it follows because ${\mathbf m}$ is bounded.] 

    2) We say ${\mathbf m}$ is strongly $\mu$-directed (or $(< \mu)$-directed; if $\mu = \aleph_{0}$ we may omit it) \underline{when}: for every $L \subseteq L_{{\mathbf m}}$ of cardinality $< \mu$ there is $t \in M_{{\mathbf m}}$ such that $L \in {\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf m}, t}$ (the condition implies ``${\mathbf m}$ is weakly bounded'' and ``${\mathbf m}$ is not lean, $t \notin M_{{\mathbf m}}^{\rm{lean}}$ when $E_{{\mathbf m}}''$ has at least two equivalence classes''). 
    
    3) We say ${\mathbf m}$ is reasonable \underline{when}: 
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(\alpha)$] ${\mathbf m}$ is strongly $\lambda^{+}$-directed and $M_{{\mathbf m}}^{\rm{fat}}$ is cofinal in $M_{{\mathbf m}},$
        
        \item[$(\beta)$] ${\mathbf m}(\leq t) \in  {\mathbf M}_{\rm{ec}}$ for every $t \in M_{{\mathbf m}},$
        
        \item[$(\gamma)$] ${\mathbf m}$ is wide and bounded (see Definition \ref{c5}(10) and Definition \ref{c39}(1A)). 
    \end{enumerate}

    We define $ \mathbf{m} $ as follows:
    
    \begin{enumerate} 
    \item[$(*)_1$]   
    
        \begin{enumerate} 
            \item[(a)]  $ L_ \mathbf{m} $ as a set is  $ L_{\mathbf{m} _1} \cup L   _{\mathbf{m}_2}$,
            
            \item[(b)] $\le _ \mathbf{m} $ is the transitive closure of $ \{ (s,t):  L_{\mathbf{m} _1 } \models s < t $ or $  L_{\mathbf{m} _2 } \models s < t   \} $,
            
            \item[(c)]  $ M_ \mathbf{m} = M_  {\mathbf{m} _1} $, $M_{{\mathbf m}}^{\rm{lean}} = M_{{\mathbf m}_{1}}^{\rm{lean}}, M_{{\mathbf m}}^{\rm{fat}} = M_{{\mathbf m}_{1}}^{\rm{fat}},$
            
            \item[(d)] $ u_{\mathbf{m}, t }$ is:
               \begin{enumerate} 
                    \item[$ (\alpha ) $] $ u_{\mathbf{m} _1, t }$   when $ t \in L_{\mathbf{m} _1} \setminus L_*,$  and,
                    
                    \item[$ ( \beta ) $]  $ u_{\mathbf{m} _2, t}$  when  $ t \in L_{\mathbf{m}_2} \setminus M_{{\mathbf m}_{0}},$
                    
                    \item[$(\gamma)$] $u_{{\mathbf m}_{1}, t} \cup u_{{\mathbf m}_{2}, t}$ if $t \in M_{{\mathbf m}_{0}}.$
                \end{enumerate}
           
            \item[(e)] ${\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf m}, t}$ is:
            
            \begin{enumerate}
                \item[$(\alpha)$] ${\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf m}_{1}, t}$ when $t \in L_{{\mathbf m}_{1}} \setminus L_{*}$ and,
                
                \item[($\beta$)] ${\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf m}_{2}, t}$ when $t \in L_{{\mathbf m}_{2}} \setminus M_{{\mathbf m}_{0}},$
                
                \item[$(\gamma)$] $[u_{{\mathbf m}, t}]^{\leq \lambda}$ if $t \in M_{{\mathbf m}_{0}}^{{ \rm fat}},$
                
                \item[$(\delta)$] ${\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf m}_{1}, t} \cup {\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf m}_{2}, t}$ if $t \in M_{{\mathbf m}_{0}} \setminus M_{{\mathbf m}_{\gamma}}^{{ \rm fat}}.$
            \end{enumerate}
            
            \item[(f)]   We define $ E'_\mathbf{m} $ by: for $ s,t \in L_ \mathbf{m} $,  we have $ s E'_{{\mathbf m}} t $  \underline{iff} $ s E'_{\mathbf{m} _1} t$  or $ s E'_{\mathbf{m} _2 } t.$
        \end{enumerate} 
    \end{enumerate}
     
     As  $L _* $  is an initial segment of $ L_{\mathbf{m} _1 }$  we have:
                
    \begin{enumerate}

        \item[$(*)_{3}$] $L_{{\mathbf m}_{2}}$ is an initial segment of $L_{{\mathbf m}}.$

\label{b47}
    Assume $\mathbf{m} \in \mathbf{M}.$ 

    1) A sufficient condition for $ \mathbf{m} \in  {\mathbf M}_{\rm{bec}}$ is:
    
    \begin{enumerate} 
         \item[$(*)_\mathbf{m} $] For some $\delta, 
         \bar{L}, \bar{ c }$  we have:
         
         \begin{enumerate} 
             \item[(a)]  $ \bar{c} = \langle c_ \alpha: \alpha < \delta  \rangle 
             \in {}^{ \delta } (M_{\mathbf{m}}),$ 
             
             \item[(b)]  $ \bar{ L } = \langle L_ \alpha : \alpha < \delta  \rangle $, 
             
             \item[(c)] $ \mathbf{m} {\restriction} L_{\alpha} $ belongs to   $ \mathbf{M} _{{\rm ec}}$  for every $ \alpha < \delta $,
                    
             \item[(d)]  $ L_ \alpha \subseteq L_{\mathbf{m}, < c_ \alpha },  L_ \alpha \subseteq  u_{\mathbf{m} , c_ \alpha }$, $M_{{\mathbf m} (< c_{\alpha})} \subseteq L_{\alpha}$ and if $t \in L_{\alpha} \setminus M_{{\mathbf m}}$ then $L_{\alpha} \cap (t / E_{{\mathbf m}})$ is an initial segment of $t / E_{{\mathbf m}},$             
            
             \item[(e)] $ \delta $ has cofinality $> \lambda,$
             
             \item[(f)] $ \bar{ c } $ is  increasing  and cofinal in $ L_ \mathbf{m}$,
             
             \item[(g)] $ \bar{L} $  is $ \subseteq $-increasing with union $ L_ \mathbf{m} $. 
         \end{enumerate} 
    \end{enumerate} 
    
    2)  A sufficient condition for $ \mathbf{m} \in \mathbf{M}_{\rm{bec}}$ is:
    
    \begin{enumerate} 
         \item[$(*)'_\mathbf{m} $] For some $ \bar{ c}, \bar{L}$  we have:   
             \begin{enumerate} 
                \item[(a)-(e)]  as above,
                
                \item[(f)]  if $ L \subseteq L_ \mathbf{m} $ has cardinality  $ \le \lambda $ then for some $ \alpha < \delta $ we have $ L \subseteq L_{\alpha }$,   
             \end{enumerate} 
     \end{enumerate} 

    3)  For  $ L_* \subseteq L_ \mathbf{m} $  we have $(A)_{L_*} \Rightarrow (B)_{L_*},$ where:
        
    \begin{enumerate} 
        \item[$(A)_{L_*}$]   if $ L \subseteq L_* $ has cardinality  $\le \lambda $   and $ \mathbf{m} \le _\mathbf{M} \mathbf{n} $  then  $ \mathbb{P} _{\mathbf{n} }[L] = \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m} [L],$
        
        \item[$(B)_{L_*}$]  if $ \mathbf{m} \le _\mathbf{M} \mathbf{n} $  then  $ \mathbb{P} _{\mathbf{n} }[L_*] = \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m} [L_*]$,   
    \end{enumerate} 

    4) If $ c \in L_ \mathbf{m}, $  $ L_*  \subseteq u_{\mathbf{m}, c }$,   $ \mathbf{m} {\restriction} L_{*} \in \mathbf{M} _ {{\rm ec}},$ $M_{{\mathbf m}(< c)} \subseteq L_{*}$ and  $t \in L_{{\mathbf m}} \setminus M_{{\mathbf m}} $ implies $ \ L_{*} \cap  (t / E_{{\mathbf m}})$ is an initial segment of $t / E_{{\mathbf m}}$ \underline{then} clause $ (B)_{L_*}$ above holds, 
    
    5) We have $ (a) \Rightarrow (b),$  when:
    
    \begin{enumerate} 
        \item[(a)]  we have: 
        
            \begin{enumerate} 
                \item[$ ( \alpha ) $] ${\mathbf m}$ is strongly $(<\lambda^{+})$-directed,
                
                \item[$ ( \beta ) $] for every $t \in M_{{\mathbf m}}$ (or just for cofinally many $t \in M_{{\mathbf m}}$) we have ${\mathbf m}(\leq t) \in {\mathbf M}_{\rm{ec}}.$
            \end{enumerate}
        
        \item[(b)] ${\mathbf m} \in {\mathbf M}_{\rm{ec}}.$

    \begin{enumerate}

\label{e24}
    Assume $\mathbf m \in \mathbf M$.
    
    1) Let ${\mathscr Y}_{\mathbf m}$ be the set of pairs $(t,\bar s)$ such that  $t \in L_{\mathbf m} \backslash M_{\mathbf m}$ and $\bar s \in 
    {}^\zeta(t/E''_{\mathbf m})$ for some $\zeta < \lambda^+$;  we may write $\bar s$ instead of $(t,\bar s)$  as usually $\bar s$ determines $t/E''_ \mathbf{m} $,  but this is the only information  about $t$  that matter.  We could have used instead pairs  $ (t/E''_\mathbf{m} , \bar{s})$.
          
    2)  By induction on the ordinal $\gamma$ we define when  $(t_1,\bar s_1),(t_2,\bar s_2)$ are $\gamma$-equivalent in $\mathbf m$ or are $(\mathbf m,\gamma)$-equivalent:
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)]  if $\gamma=0$, {\underline{then}} \, letting $L_\ell = (M_{\mathbf m} \cup {\rm rang}(\bar s_\ell))$ for $\ell=1,2$ there is $h$ such that: 
        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[$(\alpha)$]  $h$ is an isomorphism from $\mathbf m {\restriction} L_1$ onto $\mathbf m {\restriction} L_2$, 
            
            \item[$(\beta)$]  $h$ maps $\bar s_1$ to $\bar s_2$,
            
            \item[$(\gamma)$]  $h {\restriction} M_{\mathbf m}$ is the identity,
            
            \item[$(\delta)$]  $h$ induces an isomorphism from  ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L_1)$ onto ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L_2)$ (as defined in \ref{c4}$(*)_4(b)$),  
            
            \item[$(\varepsilon)$]  moreover, $h$ induces an isomorphism from ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}[L_1]$ onto ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}[L_2]$, as defined in \ref{b20}, so $p^*_{t,\eta} \mapsto p^*_{h(t),\eta}$, see \ref{b11}(3), 
        \end{enumerate}
        
        \item[(b)]  if $\gamma = \beta +1$ {\underline{then}} \, for every  $\ell \in \{1,2\}$ for every 
        $\varepsilon < \lambda^+$ and  $\bar s'_\ell \in {}^\varepsilon(t_\ell/E''_{\mathbf m})$  there is  $\bar s'_{3 - \ell} \in {}^\varepsilon(t_{3 - \ell}/E''_{\mathbf m})$ such that $(t_1,\bar s_1 \char 94 \bar s'_1),(t_2,\bar s_2 \char 94 \bar s'_2)$ are $\beta$-equivalent, 
        
        \item[(c)]  if $\gamma$ is a limit ordinal {\underline{then}} \, $(t_1,\bar s_1), (t_2,\bar s_2)$ are $\beta$-equivalent for every $\beta < \gamma$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-17 -->

\label{e27}
    For $\mathbf m \in \mathbf M$ and ordinal $\alpha$ the number of equivalence classes of ``being $(\mathbf m,\alpha)$-equivalent" is $\le \beth_{1 +\alpha +1}(\lambda_1)$.
<!-- end claim-18 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
y induction on $\alpha$.
    
     
    \underline{Case 1}:  $\alpha = 0$:
    
    Note that the set of elements of ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(M_{\mathbf m} \cup {\rm rang}(\bar s))$ has cardinality $\le 2^{\lambda_1}$ (and even $\le
    (\lambda_1)^\lambda$) and depends just on $\mathbf m {\restriction} (M_{\mathbf m} \cup {\rm rang}(\bar s))$ but there are $\beth_2(\lambda_1)$  possibilities for the quasi order on ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L_1)$ and even for ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}[L_1]$.  
    
    \underline{Case 2}:  $\alpha$ is a limit ordinal:
    
    By clause (c) of Definition \ref{e24}, the number of $\alpha$-equivalence classes is $\le \prod\limits_{\beta < \alpha}$ (the
    number of $\beta$-equivalence classes) 
    $\le \prod\limits_{\beta < \alpha} \beth_{1 + \beta +1} (\lambda_1) \le  (\beth_{1 + \alpha +1}(\lambda_1))^{\beth_{1 + \alpha}} = 
    \beth_{1 + \alpha +1}(\lambda_1)$.
    
    \underline{Case 3}:  $\alpha = \beta +1$:
    
    Clearly every $\alpha$-equivalence class can be coded as a set of $\beta$-equivalence classes hence the number of $\alpha$-equivalence
    classes is $\le 2^{\beth_{1 + \beta +1}(\lambda_1)}  = \beth_{1 + \beta +2}(\lambda_1) = \beth_{1 + \alpha +1}(\lambda_1)$, as promised.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- definition-18: body_md -->
\label{e28}
    For an ordinal $\beta$, let ${\mathscr G}_{\mathbf m,\beta}$ be the set of  functions $f$ such that for some $t^\ell_i,\bar s^\ell_i$ for $i<i(*)$ and $\ell \in \{1,2\}$ we have:
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)]  $i(*) < \lambda^+$,  
        
        \item[(b)]  $\langle t^\ell_i:i < i(*)\rangle$ is a sequence of pairwise non-$E''_{\mathbf m}$-equivalent members of $L_{\mathbf m} \backslash M_{\mathbf m}$,  
          
        \item[(c)]  $\bar s^\ell_i \in {}^{\zeta(i)}(t^\ell_i/E''_{\mathbf m})$ where $\zeta(i) < \lambda^+$, 
          
        \item[(d)]  $(t^1_i,\bar s^1_i),(t^2_i,\bar s^2_i)$ are $\beta$-equivalent (members of ${\mathscr Y}_{{\mathbf m}}$), 
          
        \item[(e)]  $f$ is an isomorphism from $\mathbf m {\restriction} L_1$ onto $\mathbf m {\restriction} L_2$ when $L_\ell = \cup\{{\rm rang}(\bar s^\ell_i):i < i(*)\} \cup M_{\mathbf m}$, 
          
        \item[(f)]  $f {\restriction} M_{\mathbf m} =$ the identity, 
        
        \item[(g)]  $f$ maps $\bar s^1_i$ to $\bar s^2_i$ for $i<i(*)$.
    \end{enumerate}
    
    
    2) For $f \in {\mathscr G}_{\mathbf m,0}$ we define $\hat f$ as the mapping from   ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}({\rm dom}(f))$ onto ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}({\rm rang}(f))$ induced by $f$; see clause \ref{e24}(2)(a)$(\varepsilon)$;  (clearly well defined 1-to-1 function, but does it preserve the order? we shall return to this in \ref{e33}).
<!-- end definition-18 -->

\label{e31} 
    1) In \ref{e29}(1)  instead of $ {\rm stt} _{p,q,\psi}$ we  can use the stronger statement: 
    
    \begin{enumerate} 
        \item[$({\rm stt})'_{p,q,\psi}$] as there but  omit
        clause (d) and add to clause (c): also  $\varphi,q$ are compatible in ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}[L_{\mathbf m}]$, 
     \end{enumerate} 
     
    But the present choice is more convenient in the proof of \ref{e29}(1).
    
    2) We use $\lambda > \aleph_0$ in the proof, to eliminate it we can imitate the completeness theorem\footnote{but we give details. First as a warm up notice that (for $\lambda = \aleph_{0})$: 

    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(\ast)$] if $r \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ \underline{then} we can find ${\mathscr T}$ and $\bar{r}, \bar{s}$ such that:  
    \end{enumerate}
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)]  
        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[$(\alpha)$] ${\mathscr T}$ is a sub-tree of ${}^{\omega >} \omega$ which is well founded,
        
            \item[($\beta$)] if $\eta \in {\mathscr T},$ \underline{then} ${\rm suc}_{{\mathscr T}}(\eta)$ is empty or is $\omega.$  
        \end{enumerate}
        
        \item[(b)] $\bar{r} = \langle r_{\eta}: \eta \in {\mathscr T} \rangle$ and $r_{\langle \rangle} = r,$
        
        \item[(c)] $r_{\eta} \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ and $r_{\eta} \subseteq r_{\nu}$ for $\eta \unlhd \nu \in {\mathscr T},$
        
        \item[(d)] $\bar{s} = \langle s_{\eta}: \eta \in {\mathscr T} \setminus \max({\mathscr T}) \rangle$ such that $\eta \lhd \nu \Rightarrow s_{\nu} \nleq s_{\eta},$
        
        \item[(e)] if $\eta = \nu^{\smallfrown} \langle k \rangle \in {\mathscr T},$ \underline{then} $s_{\nu} \in {\rm dom}(r_{\nu}) \cap M_{{\mathbf m}}$ and $r_{\nu} {\restriction} ({\rm dom}(r_{\nu}) \setminus L_{{\mathbf m}(\leq s_{\nu})}) = r_{\eta} {\restriction} ({\rm dom}(r_{\nu}) \setminus L_{{\mathbf m}(s_{\nu})}),$
        
        \item[(f)] if $ \eta \in \max({\mathscr T}),$ \underline{then} ${\rm dom}(r_{\eta}) \cap M_{{\mathbf m}} = \{ s_{\eta {\restriction} \ell}: 0 < \ell \leq \lg(\eta)  \},$
        
        \item[(g)] if $\eta \in {\mathscr T} \setminus \max({\mathscr T}),$ \underline{then} for some $k$ we have: 
        
        \begin{itemize}
            \item if $\ell \geq k,$ then ${\rm tr}(r_{\eta^{\smallfrown} \langle i \rangle}(s_{\eta}))$ has length $\ell,$
            
            \item if $\ell \geq k, \varrho = {\rm tr}(r_{\eta^{\smallfrown} \langle i \rangle}(s_{\eta}))$ for some $\varrho \in \Pi_{{\varepsilon} < \ell} \theta_{{\varepsilon}},$ \underline{then} for every $\rho \in \Pi_{{\varepsilon} < \ell} \theta_{{\varepsilon}}$ satisfying $\varrho \leq \ell$ and ${\rm tr}(r_{\eta}(s_{\eta})) \unlhd \rho$ for some $j < \omega$ we have $\rho = {\rm tr}(r_{\eta^{\smallfrown} \langle j \rangle}(s_{\eta})).$ 
        \end{itemize}
    \end{enumerate}
    
    This can be proved by induction on $\sup \{ \rm{rk}(M_{{\mathbf m}}(s)) + 1: s \in {\rm dom}(r) \cap M_{{\mathbf m}} \}.$
    
    Let $\langle s_{i}: i < i_{\ast} \rangle$ lists $M_{{\mathbf m}}$ such that $s_{i} <_{{\mathbf m}} s_{j} \Rightarrow i < j,$ and let $s_{i_{\ast}} = \infty.$ For $i \leq i_{\ast}$ let $L_{i} = \bigcup \{ L_{{\mathbf m}(\leq s_{j})}: j < i \},$ it is as an initial segment of $L_{{\mathbf m}}.$ We prove by induction on $i \leq i_{\ast}$ that the statement holds when $p, q \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}(L_{i}).$ For $i = 0$ this is trivial and limit $i$ it is. So assume $i = j+1,$ now if $s_{i} \notin {\rm dom}(p) \cup {\rm dom}(q)$ this is trivial and if $s_{j} \in {\rm dom}(p) \setminus {\rm dom}(q)$ this is obvious. Similarly if $s_{j} \in {\rm dom}(q) \setminus {\rm dom}(p).$ So assume $s_{j} = {\rm dom}(p) \cap {\rm dom}(q).$ as in the proof of \ref{e29}(1), without loss of generality ${\rm tr}(q(s_{j})) \unlhd {\rm tr}(p(s_{j})).$ As in the proof of \ref{e29}(1), for some $q_{1} \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf q}},$ we have $(\ast)_{q_{1}, p, \psi}$ and $q \leq q_{1}$ and $\lg({\rm tr}(q_{1}(s))) > \lg({\rm tr}(p(s))),$ hence ${\rm tr}(p(s)) \lhd {\rm tr}(q_{1}(s)).$ 
    
    Clearly $(\ast)_{q_{1} {\restriction} L_{j}, p {\restriction} L_{j}, \psi}$ holds, therefore $q_{1} {\restriction} L_{s}, p {\restriction} L_{s}$ are compatible in ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}},$ hence in ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}(L_{j}),$ and let $r \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}(L_{j})$ be a common upper bound. Now, $r$ forces (i.e. $\Vdash_{{\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}(L_{j})}$) then $\let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-

\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}_{q(s)} {\restriction} ( \lg({\rm tr}(q(s))), \lg({\rm tr}(p(s)))) \leq {\rm tr}(q_{1}(s)),$ hence $r \Vdash_{{\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}(L_{j})}$``$p(s), q(s)$ are compatible in $\let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3{\mathbb Q}$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}_{s_{j}}$'', therefore $r, p, q$ have a common upper bound. So we are done.} for ${\mathbb L}_{\aleph_1,\aleph_0}.$

) We choose $(p_n,q_n,\psi_n)$ by induction on $n$ such that:
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$\boxplus_n$]  
        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(a)] 
            
            \begin{enumerate}
                \item[($\alpha$)] $({\rm stt})_{p_n,q_n,\psi_n}$ holds if $n$ is even,
                
                \item[($\beta$)] $({\rm stt})_{q_n,p_n,\psi_n}$ holds if $n$ is odd,
            \end{enumerate}
            
            \item[(b)] $(p_0,q_0,\psi_0) = (p,q,\psi)$,
             
            \item[(c)] if $n=2m+1$ and $s \in {\rm dom}(p_{2m}) \cap M_{\mathbf m},$ {\underline{then}} \, $s \in {\rm dom}(q_{2m+1})$,  and ${\rm tr}(p_{2m}(s)) \triangleleft {\rm tr}(q_{2m+1}(s))$, 
            
            \item[(d)] if $n=2m+2$ and $s \in {\rm dom}(q_{2m+1}) \cap M_{\mathbf m},$ {\underline{then}} \, $s \in {\rm dom}(p_{2m+2})$   and ${\rm tr}(q_{2m+1}(s)) \triangleleft {\rm tr}(p_{2m+2}(s))$, 
            
            \item[(e)] if $n=m+1$ then $p_m \le p_n,q_m \le q_n$.
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}
    
    \underline{Case 1}:  For $n=0$ use clause (b).
    
    \underline{Case 2}:   $n=2m+1$.
    
    So the triple $(p_{2m},q_{2m},\psi_{2m})$ is well defined, let $u_{2m}= {\rm dom}(p_{2m}) \cap M_{\mathbf m}$ and let $\bar\nu = \langle \nu_s:s \in u_{2m}\rangle$ be defined by $\nu_s = {\rm tr}(p_{2m}(s))$.
    
    Clearly,
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_1$]  $\psi_{2m} \Vdash p^*_{s,\nu_s}$ for $s \in u_{2m}$.
    \end{enumerate}
    
    [Why?  Clearly $p_{2m} \Vdash_{{\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}} p^*_{s,\nu_s}$, i.e. $p^*_{s,\nu_s} \le p_{2m}$ in ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}(L_{{\mathbf m}}),$ hence in ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}[L_{\mathbf m}]$ and therefore, if $\psi_{2m} \nVdash p^*_{s,\nu_s},$ then $\psi' = \psi_{2m} \wedge \neg p^*_{s,\nu_s} \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}[M_{\mathbf m}]$ is $\ge \psi_{2m}$, hence compatible with $p_{2m}$, contradiction, see clause (c) in $({\rm stt})_{p,q,\psi}$  which holds by $ \boxplus _{2m}(a)(\alpha ) $.]
    
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_2$] there is $q'_{2m} \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L_{\mathbf m})$ which is above $q_{2m}$ and above $\psi_{2m}$ and naturally $u_{2m} \subseteq {\rm dom}(q'_{2m})$ hence $s \in u_{2m}$ implies $\nu_s \subseteq {\rm tr}(q'_{2m}(s)).$
    \end{enumerate}
    
    [Why?  By clause (d) of $({\rm stt})_{p_{2m},q_{2m},\psi_{2m}}$ which holds by $\boxplus_{2m}(a)(\alpha)$ recalling ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L_{\mathbf m})$ is dense ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}[L_{\mathbf m}]$; the ``hence" by $(*)_1$.]
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_3$]  there is $\psi'_{2m} \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}[M_m]$ such that:
        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(a)]  if $\psi'_{2m} \le \varphi \in  {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}[M_{\mathbf m}]$ then $\varphi,q'_{2m}$ are  compatible in ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}[L_{\mathbf m}]$, 
            
            \item[(b)]  if $s \in u_{2m}$ then $\psi'_{2m} \Vdash p^*_{s,\nu_s}$, 
            
            \item[(c)]  $\psi_{2m} \le \psi'_{2m}$.
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}
    
    [Why?  Obvious using the $\lambda^+$-c.c., i.e. $\psi'_{2m} = \psi_{2m} \wedge \neg(\vee \{\varphi:\varphi \in {\mathscr I}\})$  where ${\mathscr I}$ is a maximal anti-chain  of members  $ \varphi 
    \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}[M_{\mathbf m}]$ satisfying
    $ \varphi  \perp q'_{2m}$ in ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}[L_{\mathbf m}];$ see more in \ref{e29}.]
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_4$]  {\rm without loss of generality} \, ${\rm wsupp}(q'_{2m}) \cap {\rm wsupp}(p_{2m}) \subseteq  M_{\mathbf m}$.
    \end{enumerate}
    
    [Why?  As $\mathbf m$ is  $ \mu $-  
    wide using an automorphism of $\mathbf m$
    which is the identity on $ {\rm wsupp} ( q_{2m}),$  i.e. by \ref{e10}. Even if ${\mathbf m}$ is fat this is fine.]
    
    Lastly, let $p_n =  p'_{2m},q_n = q'_{2m},\psi_n = \psi'_{2m}$ and check.
    
    \underline{Case 3}:  $n=2m+2.$
    
    Similar to case 2 with  the roles of the $p$'s and the $q$'s interchanged. 

    Having carried the induction we  can define $p_*$ as the upper bound of, in fact the union of 
    $\{p_n:n < \omega\}$ as in \ref{c11}(3A), in particular:
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_7$ (a)]  $({\rm dom}(p_*) = \underset{n}\bigcup \, {\rm dom}(p_n)$; in fact, also ${\rm fsupp}(p_*) = \bigcup\limits_{n} {\rm fsupp}(p_n)$ and $ {\rm wsupp} ( p_* ) = \underset{n} \bigcup \,  {\rm wsupp} (p_n)$, 
        
        \item[(b)] if  $ s \in {\rm dom}(p_*)$  and $ n $ is minimal  such that  $s \in {\rm dom}(p_n)$ then ${\rm tr}(p_*(s)) = \bigcup\limits_{k \ge n} {\rm tr}(p_k(s))$  and  $ \{  f_{p_* , \iota }: \iota < \iota (p_*)(s)\} $  is equal to $ \{{\rm tr}(p_*(s))\cup f_{p_k , \iota }{\restriction} [\lg({\rm tr}(p_*(s))), \lambda ) : \iota < \iota (p_k(s))$ for some $ k \in [n, \omega ) \} $.
    \end{enumerate}
    
    Similarly let $q_*$ be the upper bound of,
    in fact the union of  $\{q_n:n < \omega\}$ as in
    \ref{c11}(3A), so again, in particular:
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_8$ (a)]  ${\rm dom}(q_*) = \bigcup\limits_{n} {\rm dom}(q_n)$,  and  also ${\rm fsupp}(q_*) = \bigcup\limits_{n} {\rm fsupp}(q_n)$ and $ {\rm wsupp} (q_*)= \cup _n {\rm wsupp} (q_n)$, 
        
        \item[(b)] if  $s \in {\rm dom}(p_*)$    and $ n $ is minimal  such that
        $s \in {\rm dom}(q_n)$ {\underline{then}}:
        
        \begin{enumerate} 
            \item[$ \bullet _1$] ${\rm tr}(q_*(s)) =
            \bigcup\limits_{k \ge n} {\rm tr}(q_k(s))$, 
            \item[$ \bullet _2$] $ \{  f_{q_* , \iota }: \iota < \iota (q_*)(s)\} $  is equal to $ \{{\rm tr}(p_*(s))\cup  f_{p_k , \iota }{\restriction} [\lg({\rm tr}(p_*(s))), \lambda ) : \iota < \iota (q_k(s))$ for some $ k \in [n, \omega ) \} $. 
        \end{enumerate} 
    \end{enumerate}
    
    Hence, 
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_9$]  $(\rm{a}) \quad p_*,q_* \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}$, 
        
        \item[${{}}$]  $(\rm{b}) \quad {\rm dom}(p_*) \cap {\rm dom}(q_*) \subseteq M_{\mathbf m}$,  moreover, ${\rm wsupp}(p_*) \cap {\rm wsupp}(q_*) \subseteq M_{\mathbf m}$, 
        
        \item[${{}}$]  $(\rm{c}) \quad {\rm dom}(p_*) \cap M_{\mathbf m} =  {\rm dom}(q_*) \cap M_{\mathbf m}$, 
        
        \item[${{}}$]  $(\rm{d}) \quad$ if $s \in {\rm dom}(p_*) \cap M_{\mathbf m}$, equivalently, $s \in {\rm dom}(p_*) \cap {\rm dom}(q_*)$ then:  ${\rm tr}(p_*(s)) = {\rm tr}(q_*(s))$.
    \end{enumerate}
    
    [Why?  Clause (a) by properties of ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}$ and $p_n \le p_{n+1},q_n \le q_{n+1}$ see above, clause (b) as ${\rm dom}(p_{2m}) \cap {\rm dom}(q_{2m}) \subseteq M_{\mathbf m}$ as $({\rm stt})_{p_{2m},q_{2m},\psi_{2m}}$. Clause (c) by
    $\boxplus_n(c),(d)$, the first conclusion and clause (d) by $\boxplus_n(c),(d)$, the second conclusion.]
    
    It follows that $p_*,q_*$ are compatible in ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}$ but $p=p_0 \le p_*,q = q_0 \le q_*$, so $p,q$ are compatible as promised.
     
    2) Let $\psi_0 \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}} [M_ \mathbf{m} ]$ be given.  Let $p \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ be such that $p \Vdash_{{\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}} ``\psi_0[\let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3{\mathbf G}$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}] = {\rm true}"$.
     
    Let  $ {\mathscr I }_0 =  \{ \varphi :  \varphi 
    \in \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m} [ M_ \mathbf{m} ]$ 
    and $ \varphi , p $ are incompatible in   $ \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m} [L_ \mathbf{m} ] \} $
    and let $ {\mathscr I } _ 1 $ be a maximal set of pairwise  incompatible members of $ {\mathscr I }_0 $. As $ \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m} [L_ \mathbf{m} ] $ satisfies the $ \lambda ^ + $-c.c., clearly 
    $ {\mathscr I } _1 $ has cardinality at most $ \lambda $ and let $ \psi = \wedge \{  \neg  \varphi : \varphi \in {\mathscr I } _1\} $. Clearly we have:
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*) _ 1$] $\psi \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[M_{{\mathbf m}}]$ and:
    
        \begin{enumerate} 
            \item[(a)]  if $ \psi \le \varphi \in  \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m} [M_ \mathbf{m} ]  $,  then $ p, \varphi $ are compatible in $ \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m} [L_ \mathbf{m} ] $,
            
            \item[(b)] $ \psi _0 \le \psi $ in  $\mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m}[M_ \mathbf{m}]$,
        
            \item[(c)] $ \psi \le p $ in $ \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m} [L]$. 
        \end{enumerate} 
    \end{enumerate} 
    
    Let $L_0 = \cup\{t/E_{{\mathbf m}}:t \in {\rm fsupp}(p)\}
    \cup M_ \mathbf{m},$ so   $ (L_0 \setminus M_ \mathbf{m} ) /E''_\mathbf{m} $  has cardinality $ < \lambda_{0}$ and as ${\mathbf m}$ is  $ \mu $-wide, we can find $L_{\varepsilon},({\varepsilon} \in [1, \mu   ))$ as required, that is, choose an automorphism
    $\pi_{\varepsilon}$ of ${\mathbf m}$ for ${\varepsilon} <  \mu $ 
    such that $\pi_{\varepsilon} {\restriction} M_{{\mathbf m}}$  is the identity, $\langle \pi_{\varepsilon}(L_0 ) \backslash M_{{\mathbf m}}:{\varepsilon} < \mu  \rangle$ are pairwise disjoint  where we let  $\pi_0$  be  the identity 
    and so  $L_{\varepsilon} = \pi_{\varepsilon}(L)$, and let   $ p_{\varepsilon} = \hat\pi(p)$ for $ \varepsilon <  \mu $.  
    Note:
    
    \begin{enumerate}

        \item[$\bullet$]  ${\rm dom}(f) \subseteq \cup\{(t/E''_{\mathbf m}) \cap L_2:
        t \in L_2\} \cup M_{\mathbf m}$,  
      
        \item[$\bullet$]  $t \in L_1 \Rightarrow f {\restriction} (t/E_{\mathbf m} \cap L_2) = {\rm id}_{(t/E_{\mathbf m}) \cap L_2}$, 
    
        \item[$\bullet$]  if $q \in \{q_i:i < i(*)\} \cup \{p\} \cup \{p_i:i < i(*)\}$ and $t \in {\rm dom}(q) \backslash M_{\mathbf m}$ then ${\rm fsupp}(q(t)) \subseteq {\rm dom}(f)$, 
          
        \item[$\bullet$]  ${\rm rang}(f) \subseteq L_{\mathbf m_1}$.
    \end{enumerate}
    
    Let $p^* = \hat f(p)$: by $\boxplus_1(a)$ clearly clauses (a),(b) of $\boxplus_2$ holds; and the choice of the $q_i$'s   (and as $ p \le q_2 \Rightarrow  \hat{f}(p ) \le \hat{f}(q_i)$)   
    also the implication ``if" of clause (c).  The
    ``only if" of clause (c) holds by $\boxplus_1(b)$ so we are done.]

    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$\boxplus_3$]  if $p \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}$ then $p \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}$ {\underline{iff}} \, ${\rm fsupp}(p) \subseteq L_{\mathbf m_1}$.
    \end{enumerate}

    [Why?  Obvious.]
    
    Recalling Definition \ref{c34}(0)(c): 
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$\boxplus_4$]  for every ordinal $\gamma$, we have  ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma}) \lessdot 
        {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\gamma})$.
    \end{enumerate}

    [Why?  We shall prove this by induction on $\gamma$ using  $\boxplus_2 + \boxplus_3$.
    
    Note that:  
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$\boxplus_{4.1}$] 
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(a)]  $L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\gamma} \cap L_{\mathbf m_1} = L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma}$, 
            
            \item[(b)]   if $f \in {\mathscr G}   _{\mathbf m,\beta}, s \in {\rm dom}(f)$ and $\beta$ is an ordinal then:
            
            \begin{itemize}
                \item   $s \in L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma}
                  \Leftrightarrow f(s) \in L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\gamma}$, 
            \end{itemize}
            
            \item[(c)]   the parallel of $\boxplus_2$ holds  replacing  the pair $ (\mathbb{P} _{\mathbf{m} _1},\mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m}  )$ by the pair  $ (\mathbb{P} _{\mathbf{m} _1}(L^{\rm dq} _{\mathbf{m} _1, \gamma }), \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m}(L^{\rm dq} _{\mathbf{m} , \gamma }))$;  so  e.g.    
            $p^* \in  {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{\rm dq} _{\mathbf m_1,\gamma})$, 
            
            \item[(d)]  $L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\gamma}$ is an initial segment of $L_{\mathbf m}$, 
            
            \item[(e)]  $L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma}$ is an initial segment of $L_{\mathbf m_1}$, 
            
            \item[(f)]  ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma}) \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L_{\mathbf m_1})$, similarly for $\mathbf m$.
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}

    We shall use this freely.  The inductive proof on $\gamma$ splits to
    three cases.

    \underline{Case 1}:  $\gamma =0.$

    So, 
    
    \begin{itemize}
        \item  $E = E''_{\mathbf m} {\restriction} L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\gamma}$ is an
        equivalence relation on $L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\gamma}$, 
        
        \item   $E {\restriction} L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma} = E''_{\mathbf m_1} {\restriction}  L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma}$, 
        
        \item   if $t \in L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma}$ then $t \notin M_{\mathbf m_1},t/E'_{\mathbf m_1} = t/E'_{\mathbf m},(t/E'_{\mathbf m_1}) \cap L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma} = (t/E_{\mathbf m_1}) \cap
        L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma} = (t/E'_{\mathbf m}) \cap L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\gamma}$ initial segment of $L_{\mathbf m_1}$ and of $L_{\mathbf m}$ and ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}((t/E_{\mathbf m_1}) \cap L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma}) = {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}((t/E_{\mathbf m_1}) \cap L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma})$, 
        
        \item ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\gamma})$ is the product with $(< \lambda)$-support of $\{{\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}
        ((t/E_{\mathbf m_1}) \cap L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma}):t \in L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\gamma}\}$, 
        
        \item similarly for $\mathbf m_1$.
    \end{itemize}
    
    So the result should be clear.

    \underline{Case 2}:  $\gamma = \beta +1$
    
    Let $M_\beta = \{s \in M_{\mathbf m}:{\rm dp}  _{\mathbf m}(s)=\beta\}$, clearly:
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$\boxplus_{4.2}$]
        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(a)]  $M_\beta$ is a set of pairwise incomparable elements,
            
            \item[(b)] $s \in M_\beta \Rightarrow L_{\mathbf m_1,<s} \subseteq L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\beta} \wedge L_{\mathbf m,<s} \subseteq L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\beta}$, 
            
            \item[(c)]  $M_\beta$ is disjoint to $L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\beta},L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\beta}$, 
            
            \item[(d)]  $M_\beta \subseteq L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma}$, 
            
            \item[(e)]  $L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\beta} \cup M_\beta$ is an initial segment of $L_{\mathbf m}$, 
            
            \item[(f)]  $L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\beta} \cup M_\beta$ is an initial segment of $L_{\mathbf m_1}$.
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}

    As first half we prove:
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$\boxplus_{4.3}$]  ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\beta} \cup M_\beta) \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\beta} \cup M_\beta)$.
    \end{enumerate}
    
    Why?  Recalling $\boxplus_{4.1}(a)$, note
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(a)^{\dagger}$]   for $p,q \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\beta} \cup M_\beta)$ we have ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\beta} \cup M_\beta) \models ``p \le q"$ iff 
        ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m , \gamma} \cup M_\beta) \models ``p \le q"$.
    \end{enumerate}
    
    [Why?  Immediate by the definition of the order and the induction hypothesis.]
    
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(b)^{\dagger}$]  if $p_1,p_2 \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\beta} \cup M_\beta)$ {\underline{then}} \, $p_1,p_2$ are compatible in  ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\beta} \cup M_\beta)$ iff they are compatible in ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\beta} \cup M_\beta)$. 
    \end{enumerate}
    
    [Why?  The implication $\Rightarrow$ holds by clause $(a)^{\dagger}$.  
        
    So assume $p_3 \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\beta} \cup M_\beta)$ is a
    common upper bound of $p_1,p_2$ in ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\beta} \cup M_\beta)$ equivalently in ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}$. 
    
    Now (by clause (b) of the claim assumption) there is $f \in {\mathscr G}_{\mathbf m,1}$ (actually $ {\mathscr G} _{\mathbf{m}, 0 }$ suffices here) such that:  
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$\bullet$]   $f {\restriction} ({\rm fsupp}(p_1) \cup
        {\rm fsupp}(p_2))$ is the identity, moreover
        
        \item[$\bullet$]   $s \in {\rm wsupp}(p_1) \cup
        {\rm wsupp}(p_2) \wedge s \in {\rm dom}(f) \Rightarrow f(s) = s$,
        
        \item[$\bullet$]  ${\rm dom}(f) = \cup\{{\rm fsupp}(p_\ell):\ell = 1,2,3\}$
        
        \item[$\bullet$] ${\rm rang}(f) \subseteq L_{\mathbf m_1}$.
    \end{enumerate}
    
    Hence clearly $f {\restriction} M_\beta = {\rm id}_{M_\beta}$ so by  $\boxplus_{4.1}(b)$ we have ${\rm rang}(f) \subseteq L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\beta} \cup M_\beta$ so $\hat f(p_3) \in  {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\beta} \cup M_\beta)$.
    
    By $\boxplus_1$ the condition $\hat f(p_3)$ is a common  upper bound of $p_1,p_2$ in ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}$ and by the previous sentence also in ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\beta} 
    \cup M_\beta)$, so by clause $(a)^{\dagger}$  
    the conclusion of $(b)^{\dagger}$  holds.] 
    
    \begin{enumerate} 
    \item[$(c)^{\dagger}$]  
        If ${\mathscr I}$ is a maximal antichain in ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1} (L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\beta} \cup M_\beta)$ {\underline{then}} \, ${\mathscr I}$ 
        is a maximal antichain of ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}
        (L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\beta} \cup M_\beta)$.
    \end{enumerate}
    
    [Why?  As in the proof of clause $ (b)^{\dagger} $  and of $\boxplus_2$.]
    
    So we are done proving $\boxplus_{4.3}$.
    
    Now we return to proving $\boxplus_4$,  note
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$\boxplus_{4.4}$]  let ${\mathscr E} = \{(s_1,s_2):s_1,s_2 \in L_*$ and
          $s_1/E_{\mathbf m} = s_2/E_{\mathbf m}\}$ where $L_* = L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\gamma} \backslash (L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf
          m,\beta} \cup M_\beta)\}$,  {\underline{then}}:
        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(a)]  ${\mathscr E}$ is an equivalence relation on $L_*,$
            
            \item[(b)]  if $s_1,s_2 \in L_*$ and $s_1 \le_{L_{\mathbf m}} s_2$ then $s_1 {\mathscr E} s_2,$
            
            \item[(c)]  if $s_1,s_2 \in L_*$ and $s_1 {\mathscr E} s_2$ then  $s_1 \in L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma} \Leftrightarrow s_2 \in 
            L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma}$ (and both $\notin M_\beta$),
            
            \item[(d)]  if $s \in L_*$ then $L_{\mathbf m,<s} \subseteq L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\beta} \cup M_\beta \cup (s/{\mathscr E}),$
            
            \item[(e)]  if $s \in L_* \cap L_{\mathbf m_1}$ then  $L_{\mathbf m_1,<s} \subseteq L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\beta} \cup M_\beta \cup (s/{\mathscr E})$.
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}

    Hence let $L_0 = L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\beta} \cup M_\beta$ and $L_1 = L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma} = L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1} \cup M_\beta$ they satisfy  all the assumptions of \ref{c33s} hence its conclusion, so we are done easily proving Case 2 of $\boxplus_4$.
    
    \underline{Case 3}:  $\gamma$ is a limit ordinal
    
    Note that in this case  the set $L^{\rm dq}_{\mathbf{m} , \gamma }  \setminus \cup \{ L^{\rm dq}_{\mathbf{m}, \beta }: \beta < \gamma \} $  consist of $ s \in  L^{{\rm dq} } _{\mathbf{m},\gamma } \setminus M_ \mathbf{m} $ which are not below any elements  from   $ L^{\rm dq}_{\mathbf{m}, < \gamma } =  \cup \{L^{\rm dq}_{\mathbf{m}, \beta }: \beta < \gamma \} $  hence as in case 2 we can treat them as in the proof of  $ \boxplus _{4.4}$, citing \ref{c33s},  so we shall ignore them below.
    
    Clearly $p \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,<  \gamma})$ iff $p \in
    {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,< \gamma})$; also each of them implies $p \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,< \gamma})$. Also for $p,q \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,< \gamma})$ we have  
    ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,< \gamma}) \models ``p \le q"$ {\underline{iff}} \,
    ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,< \gamma}) \models ``p \le q"$ by the definition of the order and the induction hypothesis.  Together
    ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,< \gamma}) \subseteq  {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,< \gamma})$, (as partial orders).
    
    Next assume that $q_1,q_2 \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,< \gamma})$ and $p_3$ is a common upper bound of $q_1,q_2$ in  ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,< \gamma})$.
    
    We shall find $p_1 \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,< \gamma})$ such that:
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_1$]  $(\rm{a}) \quad p_1$ is above $q_1,q_2$ (in  ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,< \gamma})$ or equivalently in ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,< \gamma}))$,
        
        \item[${{}}$]  $(\rm{b}) \quad$ if $p_1 \le p'_1 \in  {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,< \gamma})$ then $p'_1,p_3$ are compatible in ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,< \gamma})$.
    \end{enumerate}
    
    This clearly suffices; why? e.g. if $\{r_i:i < i(*)\} \subseteq {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,< \gamma})$ is a maximal antichain of ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,< \gamma})$ but not of
    ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,< \gamma})$, let $q_1 = q_2 = \emptyset$ and $p_3 \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,< \gamma})$ be incompatible with every $r_i$; let $p_1$ be as in $(*)_1$, it gives a contradiction.
    
    If ${\rm cf}(\gamma) \ge \lambda$ then for some $\gamma_1 < \gamma$ we have $q_1,q_2 \in {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma_1})$ and ${\rm fsupp}(p_3) \cap L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,< \gamma} \subseteq L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\gamma_1}$ and use the induction hypothesis on $\gamma_1$ for
    clause (a) of $(*)_1$; for clause (b) of $(*)_1$ we also recall \ref{c11}(6); (alternatively imitate the case ${\rm cf}(\gamma) < \lambda$, choosing ``changing our minds" $\gamma_{\varepsilon} < \gamma$ with the induction).  So assume $\aleph_0 \le {\rm cf}(\gamma) < \lambda$ and let $\langle \gamma_\varepsilon:\varepsilon < {\rm cf}(\gamma)\rangle$ be increasing continuous with limit $\gamma$.
    
    Now we choose $p_{1,\varepsilon}$ by induction on $\varepsilon \le {\rm cf}(\gamma)$ such that:
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_2$]
    
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(a)]  $p_{1,\varepsilon} \in 
            {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m_1,\gamma_\varepsilon})$, 
            
            \item[(b)]  $(\gamma_\varepsilon,q_1 {\restriction} L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\gamma_\varepsilon},q_2 {\restriction} L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\gamma_\varepsilon},p_3 {\restriction} L^{{\rm dq}}_{\mathbf m,\gamma_\varepsilon},p_{1,\varepsilon})$ are like $(\gamma,q_1,q_2,p_3,p_1)$ in $(*)_1$, 
            
            \item[(c)]  $p_{1,\zeta} \le p_{1,\varepsilon}$ for $\zeta < \varepsilon$, 
            
            \item[(d)]  if $\varepsilon = \zeta +1$ and $s \in {\rm dom}(p_{1,\zeta})$ then $\ell g({\rm tr}(p_\varepsilon(s)) > {\rm cf}(\gamma)$. 
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}
    
    So we are done proving $\boxplus_4$.]

    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$\boxplus_5$]   ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_1} \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}$.
    \end{enumerate}
    
    [Why?  By $\boxplus_4$ for $\gamma$ large enough.]
    
    So we are done.
<!-- end proof-32 -->

e choose $\chi$ large enough and $\mathbf m_* \in \mathbf M_\chi$ which is wide, belongs to $\mathbf M_{{\rm ec}}$ and $\mathbf m \le_{\mathbf M} \mathbf m_*$; moreover is full and very wide (see \ref{e4}(1), as constructed in \ref{c41}).

    \begin{enumerate}

    such that $(t_\alpha,\bar s_\alpha) \in {\mathscr Y}_{\mathbf m_*},t_\alpha \in L_{\mathbf m_*} \backslash M_{\mathbf m_*},\langle t_\alpha/E_{\mathbf m}:\alpha < \lambda_2\rangle$ are pairwise distinct and for every $(t,\bar s) \in {\mathscr Y}_{\mathbf m_*}$ there are $\lambda^+$ ordinals $\alpha < \lambda_2$ such that $(t,\bar s),(t_\alpha,\bar s_\alpha)$ are $\xi$-equivalent, possible by \ref{e27} recalling $\lambda_2 \ge \beth_3(\lambda_1)$.   Let $L' = \cup\{t_\alpha/E_{\mathbf m_*}:\alpha <
    \lambda_2\} \cup L_{\mathbf m}$ and for each $t \in L' \backslash M_{\mathbf m_*}$ let $\langle s_{t,\alpha}:\alpha < \lambda^+\rangle$ be
    such that $s_{t,\alpha} \in L_{\mathbf m_*} \backslash M_{\mathbf m_*}$ and $\mathbf m_* {\restriction} (s_{t,\alpha}/E_{\mathbf m_*})$ is isomorphic to
    $\mathbf m_* {\restriction} (t/E_{\mathbf m_*})$ over $M_{\mathbf m}$.  Let $L = L' \cup \{s_{t,\alpha}:\alpha < \lambda^+,t \in  L' \backslash M_{\mathbf m_*}\}$ and $\mathbf n = \mathbf m_* {\restriction} L$.  Now it is easy to check that $\mathbf n$ is as required.] 
    
    It suffices to prove that $\mathbf n$ belongs to $\mathbf M_{{\rm ec}}$, let
    $\mathbf n \le_{\mathbf M} \mathbf n_1 \le_{\mathbf M} \mathbf n_2$.
    
    {\rm Without loss of generality} \, $L_{\mathbf n_2}$ has cardinality  $\le 2^{\lambda_2}$, by the LST argument;  (what is the LST argument here? let $ \chi _*$  be large enough such that $ \lambda, \mathbf{m}, \mathbf{m}_*,  \mathbf{n}_1, \mathbf{n} _2 $ all   belong to $ {\mathscr H} ( \chi _*)$ and let $ \mathfrak{A} \prec  ({\mathscr H}(\chi _*), \in ) $  be of cardinality $2^\lambda_{2}$    such that all  the above belong to it and  $ u \subseteq  \mathfrak{A} \wedge |u| \le  \lambda _2 \Rightarrow u \in \mathfrak{A} $. Now replace  $ \mathbf{n} _1, \mathbf{n} _2 $ by their restriction  to $ \mathfrak{A}  $). 
        
     
    Now as $\mathbf m_*$ is very wide and full {\rm without loss of generality} \, $\mathbf n_2 \le_{\mathbf M} \mathbf m_*$.  Now $(\mathbf n_1,\mathbf m_*)$ 
    satisfies the criterion from \ref{e35} hence ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_1} \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_*}$.
    
    Also the pair $(\mathbf n_2,\mathbf m_*)$ satisfies the criterion from \ref{e35} looking at the criterion.  Hence by \ref{e35} we have ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2} \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m_*}$.
    
    As $\mathbf n_1 \le_{\mathbf M} \mathbf n_2 \le_{\mathbf M} \mathbf m_*$ from the last two sentences it easily follows that ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_1} \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n_2}$, so we are done.

\label{e47}
    Assume $\mathbf m \in \mathbf M_{\le \lambda_2}$ and $M $  is a subset of $ M_{\mathbf m}$.
    
    1) $\mathbf n := \mathbf m \langle M \rangle$ indeed belongs to $\mathbf M$ and is equivalent to $\mathbf m$ hence ${\mathbb P}_{\mathbf m}(L_{\mathbf m}) = {\mathbb P}_{\mathbf n}(L_{\mathbf m})$ i.e. ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}} = {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}.$ 
    
    2) If $\mathbf n  = \mathbf{m} \langle M \rangle  
    \le_{\mathbf M} \mathbf n_1$ {\underline{then}} \, for some $\mathbf m_1$ we have $\mathbf m \le_{\mathbf M} \mathbf m_1$ and $\mathbf m_1,\mathbf n_1$ are equivalent.

) Check, noting that $t \in L_{\mathbf n} \backslash M_{\mathbf n} \Rightarrow t \in L_{\mathbf m} \backslash M \Rightarrow |t/E'_{\mathbf n}| \le |L_{\mathbf n}| = |L_{\mathbf m}| \le \lambda_2$ and $|M_{\mathbf m}| = |M| \le |M_{\mathbf m}| \le \lambda_1$, (in fact, here $ M \subseteq M_ \mathbf{m} $ is not necessary,  only $ `` M $ has cardinality $ \le \lambda_1 "$).
    
    2) Given such $\mathbf n_1$ we now define $\mathbf m_1 \in \mathbf M$ by: 
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_1$]
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(a)]  $L_{\mathbf m_1} = L_{\mathbf n_1}$,
            
            \item[(b)]  $\bar u_{\mathbf m_1} = \bar u_{\mathbf n_1}$ and $\bar{{\mathscr P}}_{\mathbf m_1} = \bar{{\mathscr P}}_{\mathbf n_1}$, 
            
            \item[(c)]  $M_{\mathbf m_1} = M_{\mathbf m}$,

        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}
    
    Clearly:

    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(*)_2$] 
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(a)]  $\langle M_{\mathbf m}\rangle \char 94 \langle s/E''_{\mathbf m}:s \in L_{\mathbf m_1} \backslash M_{\mathbf m} \rangle \char 94 \langle t/E''_{\mathbf n_1}:t \in L_{\mathbf n_1} \backslash L_{\mathbf n}\rangle$ is a partition of $L_{\mathbf m_1} = L_{\mathbf n_1}$,  
            
            \item[(b)]  $E''_{\mathbf m_1} = E'_{\mathbf m_1} {\restriction} \{(s,t) \in E'_{\mathbf m_1}$ and $s,t \notin M_{\mathbf m}\}$  is an equivalence relation, its equivalence classes  being the sets listed in clause (a) except $M_{\mathbf m}$,  
            
            \item[(c)]  $\mathbf m_1$ satisfies clause $(e)(\gamma)$ of Definition \ref{c4}. 
        \end{enumerate}

            \item[$(\gamma)$]   $u_{\mathbf m_1,s} =
                u_{\mathbf n_1,s} = 
                u_{\mathbf n,s} = u_{\mathbf m,s}$, 
                
            \item[$(\delta)$]  ${\mathscr P}_{\mathbf m_1,s} = {\mathscr P}_{\mathbf m,s}= {\mathscr P} _{\mathbf{n}_1 , s }= 
            {\mathscr P} _{\mathbf{n}, s}$. 
        \end{enumerate}
        
        \item[(b)]  if $s \in L_{\mathbf m_1} \backslash L_{\mathbf m}$ then:  
        
        \begin{enumerate}

            \item[$(\beta)$]  $s/E'_{\mathbf m_1} = s/E'_{\mathbf n_1}$, 
            
            \item[$(\gamma)$]  $u_{\mathbf m_1,s} = u_{\mathbf n_1},s$, 
            
            \item[$(\delta)$]  ${\mathscr P}_{\mathbf m_1,s} = {\mathscr P}_{\mathbf n_1,s}$.

            \setminus {\mathscr P} _{\mathbf{n}  , s })$

    and easily,

    \begin{enumerate}

        \item[(b)] $L$  is ${\mathbb L}_{\lambda_{1}^{+}, \lambda_{1}^{+}}$-definable in ${\rm md}_{\bar{t}}({\mathbf m})$ (without parameters),
        
        \item[(c)] the following are definable in ${\rm md}_{\bar{t}}({\mathbf m})$ by a formula (without parameters) in ${\mathbb L}_{\lambda_{1}^{+}, \lambda_{1}^{+}}$:
        
        \begin{itemize}

            \item $\bar{a}$ represent some $p \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}(L),$
            
            \item $\bar{a}_{1}, \bar{a}_{2}$ represent $p_{1}, p_{2} \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}(L)$ respectively, and $p_{1} \leq_{{\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}(L)}} p_{2},$
            
            \item $\bar{a}_{1}, \bar{a}_{2}$ represent $p_{1}, p_{2} \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[L]$ respectively and $p_{1} \leq_{{\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[L]} p_{2}.$
            
        \end{itemize}
    \end{enumerate}

\label{h16}
    1) The set $L = \{ s \in L_{{\mathbf m}}: \ \text{for no} \ t \in M_{{\mathbf m}} \ \text{do we have} \ t \leq_{{\mathbf m}} s \}$ is good.
    
    2) If $L$ is good and $t_{*} \in M_{{\mathbf m}} \setminus L$ but $L_{{\mathbf m}(< t_{*})} \subseteq L,$ then $L \cup \{ t_{*} \}$ is good. 
    
    3) If $\langle L_{\alpha}: \alpha < \delta \rangle$ is an $\subseteq$-increasing sequence of good sets and $\delta < \lambda_{1}^{+}$ \underline{then} so is $\bigcup_{\alpha < \delta} L_{\alpha}.$
 
    4) If $L$ is good then $L^{+} = \{ s: \text{there is no} \ t \in M_{{\mathbf m}} \setminus L \ \text{such that} \ t \leq_{{\mathbf m}} s \}$ is good.

otice that 1), 2) and 3) are straightforward. Concerning part (2) the reader may wonder: how do you define ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}(L)$ not using parameters if, say, multiple such $t_{\ast}$'s exists?. The answer is by \ref{h2}(3) clause (c); that is, each $t \in M_{{\mathbf m}}$ is definable without parameters. 
    
    4) The point is that we do not like \ to induct on $\rm{dp}(s, L_{{\mathbf m}})$ just on $\rm{dp}(t, M_{{\mathbf m}}).$ Note that the clauses on ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[L^{+}]$ follows by those on ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}(L^{+}).$ What we do is noting:
    
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[$\oplus$] for $p, q \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}(L^{+}), p \leq q$ iff:
        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(a)] $p {\restriction} L \leq_{{\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}(L)} q {\restriction} L,$
            
            \item[(b)] if $s \in {\rm dom}(p) \setminus L$ \underline{then} necessarily $s \in L^{+} \setminus L$  and $s / E_{{\mathbf m}}''$ appears in $\langle t_{\alpha} / E_{{\mathbf m}}: \alpha < \alpha_{{\mathbf m}} \rangle$ and,
            
            \begin{itemize}
                \item[$\bullet$] ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[L \cup (s / E_{{\mathbf m}})] \models p {\restriction} (L \cup (L^{+} \cap s / E_{{\mathbf m}})) \subseteq q {\restriction} (L \cup (L^{+} \cap s / E_{{\mathbf m}})).$
            \end{itemize}
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{itemize}
    
    [Why? Just think.]
    
    Recalling \ref{h2}(3)(A)(d) it suffice to prove that: 
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(\ast)$] Assume $s \in L^{+} \setminus L, p, q \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ and ${\rm dom}(p) \subseteq {\rm dom}(q) \subseteq L \cup (s / E_{{\mathbf m}}')$ \underline{then} ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}} \models$ ``$p \leq q$ iff (a) $+$ (b)'', where:
        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(a)] $(p {\restriction} L) \leq_{{\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}(L)} (q {\restriction} L),$
            
            \item[(b)] for some $\psi \in {\mathbb L}_{\lambda^{+}}[Y_{s / E_{{\mathbf m}}' \cap L}]$ we have: 
            
            \begin{enumerate}
                \item[$\bullet_{1}$] ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[L_{{\mathbf m}}] \models \psi \subseteq q,$
                
                \item[$\bullet_{2}$] $\psi \wedge q \wedge \neg p \notin {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[L^{+} \cap (s / E_{{\mathbf m}}')].$
            \end{enumerate}
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}
    
    [Why $(\ast)$ holds? As in \S3C.]

    \begin{itemize}
        \item if ${\varepsilon} \leq \zeta_{\ast},$ then $L_{2 {\varepsilon}} = \{ t \in L_{{\mathbf m}}:$ for some $\zeta < {\varepsilon}$ we have $t \leq_{L_{{\mathbf m}}} s_{\zeta} \},$
        
        \item for ${\varepsilon} \leq \zeta_{\ast}$ we let $L_{2 {\varepsilon} +1} = L_{2 {\varepsilon}} \cup \{ t \in L_{{\mathbf m}}:$ if $\zeta \in [{\varepsilon}, \zeta_{\ast})$ then $s_{\zeta} \nleq t$ \underline{or} for some $\xi < {\varepsilon}$ we have $(\forall \zeta \in [\xi, \zeta_{\ast}))(s_{\zeta} \nleq t) \}.$  
    \end{itemize}

    Pedantically, the models   $ \langle  {\rm md}( \mathbf{m} ) {\restriction} A_{\mathbf{m} , \alpha }: \alpha < \alpha _ \mathbf{m} \rangle $ are not pairwise disjoint but the common part consists  of $\lambda_{1}$ individual constants \underline{hence} this does not matter.
    
    Clearly $L_{2 \zeta_{\ast} +1} = L_{{\mathbf m}}, L_{{\varepsilon}}$ is a definable initial segment of $L_{{\mathbf m}}.$ By Definition \ref{h13} it suffice to prove that $L_{{\mathbf m}}$ is good. 
    
    Now we prove by induction on ${\varepsilon}$ that $L_{{\varepsilon}}$ is good, so for ${\varepsilon} = 2 \zeta_{\ast} +1$ we get the desired conclusion. 
    
    For $\zeta = 0,$ this holds by \ref{h16}(1).
    
    For $\zeta = 2 {\varepsilon} +1$ we have $L_{\zeta} \setminus L_{2 {\varepsilon}} = \{ s_{{\varepsilon}} \}$ and $L_{{\mathbf m}(< s_{\alpha})} \subseteq L_{2 {\varepsilon}};$ hence by \ref{h16}(2) we are done. 
    
    For $\zeta = 2 {\varepsilon} + 2$ we apply \ref{h16}(4).
    
    Lastly, for $\zeta$ limit we apply \ref{h16}(3). Together we are done. 
    
    2) By part (1) and the addition theorem, (best formulated for the intermediate logic $ \mathbb{L} _{\infty , \lambda ^+_ 1, \zeta}$ for $ \zeta < \lambda ^+_1)$,  see \cite{Dic85}). 
        
    3), 4) As in the proof of \ref{h22} below.
<!-- end proof-38 -->

\label{e51}
    Assume  $ \mathbf{m}$ is $\lambda_{0}$-wide.   Let $ \mathbb{P} ^\dagger _\mathbf{m} =  \mathbb{P} ^ \dagger_\mathbf{m} [M_ \mathbf{m} ]$     be the forcing notion $ \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m}  [M_ \mathbf{m}]$ restricted to the set of $ \psi \in \mathbb{P}_\mathbf{m} [M_\mathbf{m} ]$ such that there is $ p \in \mathbb{P} _\mathbf{m} (L_ \mathbf{m})$ witnessing it, which means that (it is the projection of $ p $ into $ \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m} [M_ \mathbf{m} ] $, that is): 
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$\bullet _1$] the condition $ \psi  $ is smaller or equal to $ p $  in the forcing notion $\mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m} [L_\mathbf{m} ],$
        
        \item[$\bullet _2$]  if $ \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m} [M_\mathbf{m}] \models ``\psi \le \varphi" $ {\underline{then}} \, $ \varphi, p $ are compatible in the forcing notion $ \mathbb{P} _\mathbf{m} [L_ \mathbf{m}].$
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-23 -->
<!-- claim-28: body_md -->
\label{e52} 
    Assume $ \mathbf{m} $ to be $\lambda_{0}$-wide.
      
    1) $\mathbb{P} ^ \dagger _ \mathbf{m} $ is a dense subset  of $ \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m} [M_\mathbf{m} ]$, hence  $ \mathbb{P} ^ \dagger _ \mathbf{m}  \lessdot \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m} [L_ \mathbf{m}]$.
    
    2) If $L$ is an initial segment of $L_{{\mathbf m}}$ and ${\mathbf n} = {\mathbf m} {\restriction} L,$ {\underline{then}} \,  $ \mathbb{P} ^ \dagger_\mathbf{n} =  \mathbb{P} ^\dagger_ \mathbf{m}  \cap  \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{n}[M_ \mathbf{n}]$. 
    
    3) If $L$ is a $\lambda_{0}$-wide initial segment of $L_ \mathbf{m}$, and $ \mathbf{n} = \mathbf{m} \upharpoonright L,$ {\underline{then}}:  
     
     \begin{enumerate} 
         \item[(a)]  $ \mathbb{P}_\mathbf{n} [M_\mathbf{n} ] \lessdot \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{n} [L_ \mathbf{n} ]$ and $ \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{n} [M_ \mathbf{n} ] = \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m} [M_\mathbf{n} ]  \lessdot \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m} [M_ \mathbf{m}]$,  
         
         \item[(b)] if $ p_1 \in \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{n} (L_ \mathbf{n} )$ \underline{then}  there is $ \psi  \in \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{n} [M_ \mathbf{n}]$ satisfying:  
         
         \begin{enumerate} 
             \item[($ \alpha $)]  $ \psi   \le p_1 \in \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{n} [L_ \mathbf{n}]$, 
             \item[($ \beta  $)] if $ \psi  \le  \varphi  \in \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{n} [M_ \mathbf{n} ] $   then $ p_1, \varphi $ are compatible  in $ \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{n} [L_ \mathbf{n}]$,
             
             \item[($\gamma$)]  $ \psi $ being witnessed by $ p_1$, (see Definition \ref{e51} this follows).
        \end{enumerate} 
    \end{enumerate}

) Let $\varphi \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[M_{{\mathbf m}}]$ and we should find $\psi \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}^{{\dagger}}$ above it,  this suffice. Clearly there is $p_{1} \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ such that $\varphi \leq p_{1},$ that is $p_{1} \Vdash$``$\varphi \in \let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3{\mathbf G}$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}_{{{\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[L_{{\mathbf m}}]}}$''. Now let $\langle \psi_{i}: i < i_{*} \rangle$ be a maximal anti-chain of members of ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}[M_{{\mathbf n}}]$ which are incompatible with $p_{1}$ in ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[L_{{\mathbf m}}].$ Clearly $i_{*} < \lambda^{+}$ hence without loss of generality $i_{*} \leq \lambda$ and let $\psi = \bigwedge_{i < i_{*}} \neg \psi_{i}.$  Clearly $p_{1}$ witnesses $\psi \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}^{{\dagger}}$ hence $\varphi \leq \psi,$ see more details in the proof of \ref{e52}(3). 
    
    2) Trivially ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}^{\dagger} \subseteq {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}[M_{{\mathbf n}}],$ so it suffice assume $\psi \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}[M_{{\mathbf n}}]$ and prove $\psi \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}^{\dagger} \Leftrightarrow \psi \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}^{\dagger}.$
    
    First assume $\psi \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}^{\dagger}$ is witnessed by $p \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}$ and we shall prove that $p$ witness $\psi \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}^{\dagger};$ we have to check the two conditions $\bullet_{1} + \bullet_{2}$ of Definition \ref{e51}. Now clearly $p \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ and $\psi \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[M_{{\mathbf m}}]$ (the second because $\psi \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[M_{{\mathbf m}}]$ and ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}} \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ and $M_{{\mathbf n}} \subseteq M_{{\mathbf m}},$ hence ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[M_{{\mathbf n}}] \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[M_{{\mathbf m}}]$). Also ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}[L_{{\mathbf n}}] \models \psi \leq p$ but ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}[L_{{\mathbf n}}] \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[L_{{\mathbf m}}]$ hence ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[L_{{\mathbf m}}] \models \psi \leq p.$ So in Definition \ref{e51} condition $\bullet_{1}$ holds; for proving condition $\bullet_{2},$ assume that ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[M_{{\mathbf m}}] \models$``$\psi \leq \varphi$'' hence, by part (1), we can find $q \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ and $\vartheta \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[M_{{\mathbf m}}]$ which is witnessed by $q$ such that $\vartheta$ is above $\varphi.$ Without loss of generality, ${\rm dom}(q) \cap  {\rm dom}(p) \subseteq M_{{\mathbf m}}$ and let $q_{1} = q {\restriction} L,$ now $q_{1}, \psi$ are compatible in ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[L_{{\mathbf m}}],$ hence in ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}[L_{{\mathbf n}}],$ also ${\rm dom}(q_{1}) \cap {\rm dom}(p)$ is included in $L = L_{{\mathbf n}}$ and is included in ${\rm dom}(q) \cap {\rm dom}(p)$ which is included in $M_{{\mathbf m}};$ together ${\rm dom}(q_{1}) \cap {\rm dom}(p) \subseteq L_{{\mathbf n}} \cap M_{{\mathbf m}} = M_{{\mathbf n}}.$  Therefore by \ref{e29}(1), $p, q_{1}$ are compatible in ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}(L_{{\mathbf m}}),$ hence in ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}(L_{{\mathbf n}})$, so let $r \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}$ be a common upper bound. As $q {\restriction} L \leq_{{\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}} r,$ clearly $r, q$ has a common upper bound $r_{1}$ (in ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$) and so $r_{1}$ is a common upper bound of $\varphi, p.$
    
    So we are done proving one implication (the ``first'' above)  and the second is easier: if $p \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ witness $\psi \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}^{\dagger},$ then $p {\restriction} L$ witness $\psi \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}^{\dagger}.$

    The first clause is obvious, the second recalling  ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}} \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ it is clear.

    \underline{Clause (b)}:

\mathpalette\oalign{$3{\mathbf G}$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}_{{\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[L_{{\mathbf n}}]}$'' hence $q_{2} \Vdash_{{\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}[L_{{\mathbf n}}]}$``$\psi \in \let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-

\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}_{{\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}[L_{{\mathbf n}}]}$''. Let $\vartheta_{*} \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}[M_{{\mathbf n}}] $ be witnessed by $ q_{2}$ (exists by part (1)) so ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}[L_{{\mathbf n}}] \models$``$\psi \leq \vartheta_{*}$''.
