    1A) Easy. 
   
    2) Toward contradiction ${\mathbf G}_{1} \neq {\mathbf G}_{2}$ so we can assume $\psi_{1} \in {\mathbf G}_{1} \setminus {\mathbf G}_{2},$ hence there is $\psi_{2} \in {\mathbf G}_{2}$ which is incompatible with $\psi_{1}.$ Without loss of generality $\psi_{1}, \psi_{2} \in {\mathbb P}^{\dagger}[M_{{\mathbf m}}].$ So there is $p_{l} \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ witnessing $\psi_{l}$ (for $l = 1, 2$), and without loss of generality ${\rm dom}(p_{1}) \cap {\rm dom}(p_{2}) \subseteq M_{{\mathbf m}}.$ 

    Now by induction on $n$ we choose \ $(\psi_{1, n}, p_{1, n}, \psi_{2, n}, p_{2, n})$ such that: 
    
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[$(*)_{n}$] for $l = 1, 2$:
        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(a)] $p_{l, n} \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}} \cap N_{{\mathbf r}}$ and $m < n \Rightarrow p_{l} \leq p_{l, m} \leq p_{l, n},$
            
            \item[(b)] $\psi_{l, n} \in {\mathbf G}_{l}$ is witnessed by $p_{l, n},$
            
            \item[(c)] $m < n \Rightarrow {\mathbb P}[M_{{\mathbf m}}] \models \psi_{l, m} \leq \psi_{l, n},$
            
            \item[(d)] ${\rm dom}(p_{1, n}) \cap {\rm dom}(p_{2, n}) \subseteq M_{{\mathbf m}},$
            
            \item[(e)] if $n = m +1, s \in {\rm dom}(p_{1, m}) \cap {\rm dom}(p_{2, m})$ then $ \max \{ \rm{lg}({\rm tr}(p_{1, m}(s))), \rm{lg}({\rm tr}(p_{2, m}(s))) \} <  \min \{ \rm{lg}({\rm tr}(p_{1, n}(s))), \rm{lg}({\rm tr}(p_{2, n}(s))) \},$
            
            \item[(f)] if $s \in {\rm dom}(p_{l, n}) \cap M_{{\mathbf m}}$ then $\eta^{p_{2, n}(s)} \lhd \nu_{s}.$
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{itemize}

    Why it is enough to carry the induction? Because for $l = 1, 2$ we can let $p_{l}$ be  the lub of the increasing sequence $\langle p_{l, n}: n < \omega \rangle,$ and now $p_{1}, p_{2}$ are  compatible (as $s \in {\rm dom}(p_{1}) \cap {\rm dom}(p_{2})$) implies $s \in {\rm dom}(p_{1, n}) \cap {\rm dom}(p_{2, n}) \cap M_{{\mathbf m}}$ for some  $n \in \omega$ which implies ${\rm tr}(p_{1}(s)) = {\rm tr}(p_{2}(s)).$
    
    Now if $q$ is a common upper bound \ $p_{1}, p_{2}$ in ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}},$ then it is a common upper bound of $\psi_{1}, \psi_{2}$ in ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[L_{{\mathbf m}}],$ contradicting the choice of $\psi_{2}.$
    
    Why can we carry the induction?

    In the induction step we use having enough automorphisms and  (reflecting to $N_{{\mathbf r}}$).
    
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[$(*)$] if $q_{1} \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}} \cap N_{{\mathbf r}}$  witnesses $\vartheta \in G_{l}$ and $\zeta < \lambda_{{\mathbf r}}$ then there are $q_{2} \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ and $\vartheta_{2} \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}^{\dagger}$ such that $\vartheta_{1} \leq \vartheta_{2}, q_{1} \leq q_{2}, q_{2}$ witnesses $\vartheta_{2}$ and $s \in {\rm dom}(q_{1}) \cap M_{{\mathbf m}} \Rightarrow \lg({\rm tr}(q_{2})) \geq \zeta.$
    \end{itemize}

    [Why? let ${\mathscr I} = \{ \varphi \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}^{\dagger}:  \text{\underline{either}} \ \varphi, \vartheta_{1} \ \text{are incompatible in} \ {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[M_{{\mathbf m}}] \ \text{\underline{or}} \ {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[M_{{\mathbf m}}] \models  \text{``}\psi_{2} \leq \varphi \text{'' and there is} \ q_{2} \in {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}} \ \text{above} \ q_{1}, s \in {\rm dom}(q_{1}) \cap M_{{\mathbf m}} \Rightarrow \lg({\rm tr}(q_{2}(s))) \geq \zeta \ \text{and} \ q_{2} \text{witnessing} \ \varphi \}$. By \ref{e29}(1), ${\mathscr I}$ is a dense subset of ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[M_{{\mathbf m}}]$ and it belongs to $N,$ so necessary ${\mathscr I} \cap {\mathbf G}_{l} \neq \emptyset$ and we can finish.]

\label{e62}
    Assume that $ \bar{p} = \langle  p_i: i < i_*
    \rangle $ where $ p_ i \in \mathbb{P} _ \mathbf{m} $ for $ i < i_*$  and $ i_{*} < \theta _0 $  (or just $ i_* < \lambda $  and $ i_* < \theta _{\lg({\rm tr}( p_i(s )))}$ for every $ i < i_*, s \in {\rm dom}(p_i)$).
    
    We define $q = \oplus (\bar{p})$ as the following function  $q$:

    \begin{enumerate} 
        \item[(A)] $ q $ is a  function with domain  $\cup \{{\rm dom}(p_i): i < i_* \}$,  
        
        \item[(B)] if $ s \in {\rm dom} (q)$ then $ q(s ) $
        is  defined as in Definition \ref{c6}, as follows  (see (c) on $ j_s  $): 
        
        \begin{enumerate} 
            \item[(a)] $ {\rm tr}(q( s ) ) = \cup \langle {\rm tr}(p_i(s ): i < j_ s$ satisfies $ s \in {\rm dom}(p_i)\rangle $,  on $ j_s $ see below, 
            \item[(b)] for $ \varepsilon \in [\lg( {\rm tr}(q( s  )),  \lambda )$ we let $f_{q}( \varepsilon ) = \sup \{p_i(s ) (\varepsilon ): i < j_s $ satisfies $ s \in {\rm dom}(p_i)\rangle\} $; pedantically we consider each of the {\text{`}\text{`}} components" of $ f_ q$; see Definition. \ref{c6}; \underline{where}:   
            
            \item[(c)]  $j_s = \sup \{j: j \leq i_{*} $ and  the set $ \{{\rm tr}(p_i(s)) : i < j $ and $s \in{\rm dom} (p_i) \} $ is a set of pairwise $ \trianglelefteq $-comparable sequences$\}$. 
        \end{enumerate} 
    \end{enumerate}

<!-- discussion-6: body_md -->
\label{g0}
    1) In the main case we have $M \subseteq M_{{\mathbf m}}$ cofinal in $M_{{\mathbf m}}$ and ${\mathbf m} {\restriction} M \cong {\mathbf m} {\restriction} M_{{\mathbf m}}.$ In \S4A we proved that if ${\mathbf m} \in M_{\rm{ec}}$ then ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[M] \cong {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[M_{{\mathbf m}}]$ even in the general case.  
    
    Our main aim is to prove more; e.g.
    
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[$(*)$]
        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(a)] for ${\mathbf m}, M$ as above,  there is ${\mathbf n} \in {\mathbf M}$ such that ${\mathbf n} = {\mathbf m} {\restriction} L_{{\mathbf n}}, M_{{\mathbf n}} = M$ and ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}} \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}},$ 
            
             \item[(b)] moreover there is ${\mathbf n}$ such that $M_{{\mathbf n}} = M, L_{{\mathbf n}} \subseteq L_{{\mathbf m}}, {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}[M] = {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[M]$ and ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[L_{{\mathbf m}}]$ is isomorphic to ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}[L_{{\mathbf n}}]$ over ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}[M].$
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{itemize}
    
    2) In the main case (${\mathbf m} \in {\mathbf M}_{{\rm ec}}$ is strongly by $\lambda^{+}$-directed even in the general case), 
    
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[$\bullet$] $\Vdash_{{\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}}$``$\{ \let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3\eta$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}_{s}: s \in M \}$ is cofinal in $(\Pi_{{\varepsilon} < \lambda} \theta_{{\varepsilon}}, <_{J_{\lambda}^{\rm{bd}}})$''. 
    \end{itemize}
    
    From Definition \ref{g2} we shall use $L' = \bigcup \rm{cmp}(M, {\mathbf m})$ defined below. 
    
    Earlier in \S3D we doctored ${\mathbf m} \in {\mathbf M}_{\leq \lambda_{2}}$ to an equivalent ${\mathbf n}$ such that $M_{{\mathbf n}} = M_{{\mathbf m}}, \, E''_{{\mathbf n}}$ has one equivalent class ``glueing'' together all $t / E_{{\mathbf n}}, t \in L_{{\mathbf m}} \setminus M_{{\mathbf m}}.$ Here things are more elaborated. First, in \ref{g2} we define the set $\rm{cmp}(M, {\mathbf m})$ of the $t / E'_{m}$  for which $M$ is enough and then  in \ref{g5} doctor ${\mathbf m}$ to an equivalent ${\mathbf n}$ with $M_{{\mathbf n}} = M,$ but glueing \ together all $t / E'_{{\mathbf n}}$ not in $\rm{cmp}(M, {\mathbf m}).$ Later we can treat ${\mathbf n}$ as earlier.
<!-- end discussion-6 -->
<!-- definition-26: body_md -->
\label{g2}
    Assume ${\mathbf m} \in {\mathbf M}$ and $M \subseteq M_{{\mathbf m}}.$
    
    1) Let $\rm{cmp}(M, {\mathbf m})$ be the set of $L$ such that for some $t \in L_{{\mathbf m}} \setminus M_{{\mathbf m}},$ we have:
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] $L = t / E_{{\mathbf m}}' = \{ s \in L_{{\mathbf m}}: s E_{{\mathbf m}}' t \},$
        
        \item[(b)] $L \cap M_{{\mathbf m}} \subseteq M.$
    \end{enumerate}

    2) Let $\rm{cmp}^{+}(M, {\mathbf m})  = \rm{cmp}(M, {\mathbf m}) \cup \{ M \}.$
    
    3) For $t_{*} \in M$ let $\rm{cmp}(t_{*}, M, {\mathbf m})$ be the set of $L \in \rm{cmp}(M, {\mathbf m})$ such that $L \subseteq L_{{\mathbf m}(\leq t_{*})}$ and similarly  $\rm{cmp}^{+}(t_{*}, M, {\mathbf m}) = {\rm cmp}(t_{\ast}, M, {\mathbf m}) \cup (M_{{\mathbf m}(\leq t_{\ast})} \cap M).$
<!-- end definition-26 -->
<!-- definition-27: body_md -->
\label{g5}
    Assume ${\mathbf m} \in {\mathbf M}, M \subseteq M_{{\mathbf m}}$ and $\mathscr{L} \subseteq \rm{cmp}(M, {\mathbf m}).$

    1) We define $\rm{rest}(\mathscr{L}, M, {\mathbf m})$ as  the object ${\mathbf n}$ consisting of (intended to be in ${\mathbf M}$):
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] the set of elements of $L_{{\mathbf n}}$ is $\bigcup \{ L: L \in \mathscr{L} \} \cup M,$
        
        \item[(b)] the order on $L_{{\mathbf m}}$ is $<_{{\mathbf m}} {\restriction} L_{{\mathbf n}},$
        
        \item[(c)] $M_{{\mathbf n}} = M,$
        
        \item[(d)] $E_{{\mathbf n}}' = E_{{\mathbf m}}' {\restriction} L_{{\mathbf n}},$
        
        \item[(e)] $u_{{\mathbf n}, s} = u_{{\mathbf m}, s} \cap L_{{\mathbf n}},$
        
        \item[(f)] ${\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf n}, s} = {\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf m}, s} \cap [u_{{\mathbf n}, s}]^{\leq \lambda}.$
    \end{enumerate}

    2) Further assume ${\mathbf m} \in {\mathbf M}_{\leq \lambda_{2}}.$ We define $\rm{Rest}(\mathscr{L}, M, {\mathbf m})$ as the object ${\mathbf n}$ consisting of (intended to be in ${\mathbf M}$):

    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] $L_{{\mathbf n}} = L_{{\mathbf m}},$
        
        \item[(b)] $M_{{\mathbf n}} = M,$
        
        \item[(c)] $E_{{\mathbf n}}' = \{ (s_{1}, s_{2}): \text{for some} \ L \in \mathscr{L}, (s_{1}, s_{2}) \in E_{{\mathbf m}}' {\restriction} L \ \text{\underline{or}} \ (\forall L \in \mathscr{L})({s_{1}, s_{2} \notin L \setminus M}), \\ \{s_{1}, s_{2} \} \subseteq L_{{\mathbf n}}, \{ s_{1}, s_{2} \} \nsubseteq M_{{\mathbf n}} \},$
        
        \item[(d)] $u_{{\mathbf n}, s} = u_{{\mathbf m}, s}$ for $s \in L_{{\mathbf n}},$
        
        \item[(e)] ${\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf n}, s} = {\mathscr P}_{{\mathbf m}, s}.$
    \end{enumerate}

    3) We may omit $\mathscr{L}$ when $\mathscr{L} = \rm{cmp}(M, {\mathbf m}).$
    
    4) For ${\mathbf r} \in {\mathbf R},$ let $\Xi_{{\mathbf r}}^{\bullet}$ be the set of $\bar{\nu}$ such that some ${\mathbf G}^{\bullet}$ witness it, which means:
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] ${\mathbf G}^{\bullet} \subseteq {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}} \cap N_{{\mathbf r}}$ is generic over $N_{{\mathbf r}},$
        
        \item[(b)] $\bar{\nu} = \langle \nu_{s}: s \in M_{{\mathbf m}} \cap N_{{\mathbf r}} \rangle,$
        
        \item[(c)] $\nu_{s} = \let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3\eta$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}_{s}[{\mathbf G}^{\bullet}]$ for $s \in M_{{\mathbf m}} \cap N_{{\mathbf r}}.$  
    \end{enumerate}
    
    (So compared to Definition \ref{e53}(2B) clause (c)($\gamma$) is not required here). 
    
    5) For ${\mathbf r} \in \mathbf{R}, M' \subseteq M_{{\mathbf m}}$ such that $ M' \in N_{{\mathbf r}}$ and $ M = M' \cap N_{{\mathbf r}},$ let $\Xi_{M}^{\bullet} = \Xi_{{\mathbf r}, M}^{\bullet}$ be the set of $\bar{\nu} = \langle \nu_{s}: s \in M \rangle$ such that some pair $({\mathbf n}, {\mathbf G})$ witnesses $\bar{\nu}$ which means: 
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(\alpha)$]  ${\mathbf n} \leq_{{\mathbf M}} \rm{rest}(M', {\mathbf m})$ and ${\mathbf n} \in N_{{\mathbf r}}$ and ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}} \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}},$
        
        \item[$(\beta)$] ${\mathbf G}$ is a subset of ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}} \cap N_{{\mathbf r}}$ generic over $N_{{\mathbf r}},$
        
        \item[$(\gamma)$] $\nu_{s} = \let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3\eta_{s}$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}[{\mathbf G}]$ for $s \in M.$
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-27 -->
<!-- claim-31: body_md -->
\label{g8}
    Assume ${\mathbf m} \in {\mathbf M}, M \subseteq M_{{\mathbf m}},$  $\mathscr{L} \subseteq \rm{cmp}(M, {\mathbf m}),$ ${{\mathbf n}_{2}} := \rm{Rest}(\mathscr{L}, M, {\mathbf m})$ (see \ref{g5}(2)) and ${\mathbf n}_{1} = \rm{rest}(\mathscr{L}, M, {\mathbf m}),$ (see \ref{g5}(1)):
    
    1) ${\mathbf n}_{1} \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf n}_{2},$ 
    
    2) $L_{{\mathbf n}_{2}} = L_{{\mathbf m}}, {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}_{2}} = {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ and $\rm{cmp}(M, {\mathbf n}_{1}) = \mathscr{L} \subseteq {\rm cmp}(M, {\mathbf n}_{2})$ and ${\rm cmp}(M, {\mathbf n}_{2}) \setminus {\mathscr{L}}$ is empty or a singleton; note that this is the single $E_{{\mathbf n}_{2}}'$-class that is not in ${\mathscr{L}}_{{\mathbf n}_{1}}.$
    
    3) If $M = M_{{\mathbf m}}$ and ${\mathscr{L}} = {\rm cmp}(M, {\mathbf m})$ then ${\mathbf n}_{1} = {\mathbf n}_{2} = {\mathbf m}.$
     
    4) if $\iota \in \{1, 2 \}$ and ${\mathbf n}_{\iota} \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf n}_{*}$ and $L_{{\mathbf n}_{*}} \cap L_{{\mathbf m}} = L_{{\mathbf n}_{\iota}},$ \underline{then} we can find ${\mathbf m}_{*}$ such that: 
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] ${\mathbf m} \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf m}_{*}$ and $L_{{\mathbf m}_{*}} = L_{{\mathbf n}_{*}} \cup L_{{\mathbf m}},$
        
        \item[(b)] $\mathscr{L} \subseteq \rm{cmp}(M, {\mathbf m}_{*}),$
        
        \item[(c)] if $\iota = 2$ then  $ {\mathbf n}_{*} = \rm{Rest}(\mathscr{L}, M, {\mathbf m}_{*}),$
        
        \item[(d)] if $\iota = 1 $ letting $\mathscr{L}_{1} = \rm{cmp}(M, {\mathbf n}_{*})$ we have ${\mathbf n}_{*} = \rm{rest}(\mathscr{L}_{1}, M, {\mathbf m}_{*}),$
        
        \item[(e)] (choosing minimal $u$) if $t \in M_{{\mathbf m}} \setminus M$ and $\iota = 1,$ then $u_{{\mathbf m}_{*}, t} = u_{{\mathbf m}, t} \cup \{ s: s \in L_{{\mathbf n}_{*}} \setminus L_{{\mathbf m}}  \ s \in u_{{\mathbf n}, t} \}.$ 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end claim-31 -->

\label{g11}
    Assume ${\mathbf m} \in {\mathbf M}.$
    
    1) If $t \in M_{{\mathbf m}}$ and ${\mathbf n} = {\mathbf m}(\leq t)$ \underline{then} $t = \max(M_{{\mathbf n}}) = \max(L_{{\mathbf n}}).$
    
    2) If  for every $t \in M_{{\mathbf m}}, \rm{rest}(M_{{\mathbf m}(\leq t)}, {\mathbf m}) \in {\mathbf M}_{\rm{{ec}}}$ \underline{then} ${\mathbf m} \in {\mathbf M}_{\rm{ec}}$ provided that  is strongly $\lambda^{+}$-directed.
    
    3) If ${\mathbf m}_{1} \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf m}_{2}$ and $ t \in M_{{\mathbf m}_{1}}$ then $\rm{rest}(M_{{\mathbf m}(\leq t), {\mathbf m}}) \leq_{{\mathbf M}} \rm{rest}(M_{{\mathbf m}(\leq t)}, {\mathbf m}).$

    1) If $L_{{\mathbf m}} = M_{{\mathbf m}}$ \underline{then} ${\mathbf m}$ is  essentially $\lambda^{+}$-directed (see Definition \ref{b36}(1)) \underline{if} $\bigcup \{ u_{s}: s \in M_{{\mathbf m}} \} = M_{{\mathbf m}} = M_{{\mathbf m}}$ and $(\{ u_{s}: s \in M_{{\mathbf m}} \}, \subseteq)$ is $\lambda^{+}-$directed.

    2) Assume ${\mathbf m}$ is strongly $\mu$-directed and ${\mathbf m}_{1} \leq {\mathbf m},$ \underline{then} ${\mathbf m}_{1}$  is strongly $\mu$-directed.

    3) if ${\mathbf m}_{1} \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf m}$ and ${\mathbf m}$ is essentially $\mu$-directed \underline{then} so is ${\mathbf m}_{1}.$

<!-- claim-33: body_md -->
\label{g14}
    1) Assume ${\mathbf m} \in {\mathbf M}_{\leq \lambda_{2}}$ is strongly $\lambda^{+}$-directed (hence bounded). There are ${\mathbf n}$ and $\bar{{\mathscr{L}}}$ such that: 
    
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[$\boxplus$] 
        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(a)] ${\mathbf m} \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf n} \in {\mathbf M}_{\lambda_{2}},$
            
            \item[(b)] ${\mathbf n} \in {\mathbf M}_{\rm{bec}},$
            
            \item[(c)] $\bar{{\mathscr{L}}} = \langle {\mathscr{L}}_{M}: M \in {\mathscr P}^{-}(M_{{\mathbf m}}) \rangle,$ recalling that for a set $X, \, {\mathscr P}(X)^{-} := \{ Y \subseteq X: Y \neq \emptyset \},$ 
            
            \item[(d)] ${\mathscr{L}}_{M} \subseteq \rm{cmp}(M, {\mathbf n})$ for $M \in {\mathscr P}^{-}(M_{{\mathbf m}})$ and ${\mathscr{L}}_{M_{{\mathbf m}}} = {\rm cmp}(M_{{\mathbf m}}, {\mathbf m}),$ 
            
            \item[(e)] ${\mathbf n}_{M} = {\mathbf n}[M] := \rm{rest}({\mathscr{L}}_{M}, M, {\mathbf m}) \in {\mathbf M}_{\rm{bec}}$ for $M \in {\mathscr P}^{-}(M_{{\mathbf m}}),$ so ${\mathbf n}_{M_{{\mathbf m}}} = {\mathbf m},$ 
            
            \item[(f)] ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}_{M}} \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}$ for $M \in {\mathscr P}^{-}(M_{{\mathbf m}}),$
            
            \item[(g)] if $t_{2} <_{{\mathbf m}} t_{3}$ are from $M_{{\mathbf m}}$ and $t_{1} \in L_{{{\mathbf n}}} \setminus L_{{\mathbf m}}$ and $(\forall s \in t_{1} / E_{{\mathbf n}}'')$ ($s <_{{\mathbf m}} t_{2}$) then $t_{1} / E''_{{\mathbf n}} \subseteq u_{{{\mathbf n}}, t_{3}}$ ({yes! not $t_{1} / E_{{\mathbf n}}'$})
            
            \item[(h)] ${\mathbf n}$ is strongly $\lambda^{+}$-directed (see \ref{b36}(2)),
            
            \item[(i)] if $M_{1} \subseteq M_{2}$ are from ${\mathscr P}^{-}(M_{{\mathbf m}})$ then $\mathscr{L}_{M_{1}} \subseteq \mathscr{L}_{M_{2}}.$
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{itemize}
    
    2) We can add: 
    
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[] 
        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(j)] if $M_{1}, M_{2} \subseteq M_{{\mathbf m}}$ and $h$ is an isomorphism from ${\mathbf m} {\restriction} M_{1}$ onto ${\mathbf m} {\restriction} M_{2}$ \underline{then} $h$ can be extended to $\hat{h},$ an isomorphism from ${\mathbf n}_{M_{1}}$ onto ${\mathbf n}_{M_{2}},$ 
            
            \item[(k)] if $M \in {\mathscr P}^{-}(M_{{\mathbf m}})$ and $L \in \mathscr{L}_{M}$ \underline{then} $L \cap L_{{\mathbf m}} \subseteq M_{{\mathbf m}}.$
            
            \item[(l)] If $M \in {\mathscr P}^{-}(M_{{\mathbf m}})$ and $h$ is an isomorphism from ${\mathbf m} {\restriction} M$ onto ${\mathbf m} {\restriction} M_{{\mathbf m}},$ \underline{then}:
            
            \begin{itemize}
                \item[$\bullet$] there is an isomorphism $\hat{h}$ from ${\mathbf n}_{M}$ onto ${\mathbf n}_{M_{{\mathbf m}}} = {\mathbf m}$ embedding $h,$
                
                \item[$\bullet$] if ${\mathbf G}^{+}$ is a subset of ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ generic over ${\mathbf V},$ then there is ${\mathbf G} \in {\mathbf V}[{\mathbf G}^{+}],$ a generic subset of ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ over ${\mathbf V}$ such that $s \in M \Rightarrow \let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3\eta$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}_{s}[{\mathbf G}^{+}] = \eta_{h(s)}[{\mathbf G}].$
            \end{itemize}
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{itemize}
    
    3) Above ${\mathbf n}$ is reasonable (see Definition \ref{e36}).

<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
) Let $\langle M_{\alpha}: \alpha < \alpha_{*} < \lambda_{1}^{+} \rangle$ list ${\mathscr P}^{-}(M_{{\mathbf m}})$ so $\alpha_{*} <   \lambda_{2}$ such that $t_{\alpha} <_{{\mathbf m}} t_{\beta} \Rightarrow \alpha < \beta.$ 
    
    We choose by induction on $\alpha \leq \alpha_{*}, {\mathbf m}_{\alpha}$ and if $\alpha < \alpha_{*},$ also ${\mathbf n}_{\alpha}^{0}, {\mathbf n}_{\alpha}^{1}, {\mathscr{L}}_{\alpha}$ such that:    
    
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[$(*)_{0}$] 
        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(a)] ${\mathbf m}_{\alpha} \in {\mathbf M}_{\leq \lambda_{2}},$
            
            \item[(b)] ${\mathbf m}_{\alpha}$ is $\leq_{{\mathbf M}}$-increasing continuous,
            
            \item[(c)] ${\mathbf m}_{0} = {\mathbf m},$
            
            \item[(d)] if $\alpha = \beta + 1,$ then: 
            \begin{enumerate}
                \item[$(\alpha)$] ${\mathbf n}^{0}_{\beta} = {\mathbf m} {\restriction} M_{\beta},$
                
                \item[$(\beta)$] ${\mathbf n}^{0}_{\beta} \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf n}^{1}_{\beta} \in {\mathbf M}_{\rm{bec}},$
                
                \item[$(\gamma)$] ${\mathbf n}_{\beta}^{1} \in {\mathbf M}_{\leq \lambda_{2}}$ and $L_{{\mathbf n}_{\alpha}^{1}} \cap L_{{\mathbf m}_{\beta}} = L_{{\mathbf n}_{\beta}^{0}},$
                
                \item[$(\delta)$] ${\mathbf n}^{1}_{\beta} = \rm{rest}({\mathscr{L}}_{\beta}, M_{\beta}, {\mathbf m}_{\alpha}),$
                
                \item[$({\varepsilon})$] if $t \in M_{{{\mathbf m}}} \setminus \cup \{ M_{\gamma}: \gamma \leq \beta \},$ then $u_{{\mathbf m}_{\alpha}, t} = u_{{\mathbf m}_{\beta}, t} \cup \{ s \in L_{{\mathbf m}_{\alpha}}: s \notin L_{{\mathbf m}_{\beta}}, s{\restriction} E_{{\mathbf m}_{\alpha}}' \subseteq L_{{\mathbf m}_{\alpha(\leq t)}} \}.$
            \end{enumerate}
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{itemize}
    
    Why can we carry the induction?
    
    First, arriving to $\alpha$ we choose ${\mathbf m}_{\alpha}$ as follows: 
    
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[$\bullet$] if $\alpha = 0$ let ${\mathbf m}_{\alpha} = {\mathbf m}$ (so $(*)(c)$ holds).
        
        \item if $\alpha$ is a limit ordinal then ${\mathbf m}_{\alpha} = \cup \{ {\mathbf m}_{\beta}: \beta < \alpha \},$ see \S1A, noting ${\mathbf m}_{\alpha} \in {\mathbf M}_{\leq \lambda_{2}}$ because $\alpha \leq \alpha_{*} < \lambda_{2}.$
        
        \item  if $\alpha = \beta + 1$ so ${\mathbf n}_{\beta}^{0}, {\mathbf n}_{\beta}^{1}$ have been chosen then choose ${\mathbf m}_{\alpha}$ by \ref{g8}(4) and $(*)(d)({\varepsilon}).$
    \end{itemize}
    
    Second assuming $\alpha < \alpha_{*},$ and ${\mathbf m}_{\alpha}$ has been defined we choose ${\mathbf n}_{\alpha}^{0}$ as $\rm{rest}(M_{\alpha}, {\mathbf m}_{\alpha})$ so ${\mathbf n}_{\alpha}^{0} \in {\mathbf M}_{\leq_{\lambda_{2}}}$ by \ref{g8}(1), so $(*)(d)(\alpha)$ holds.  Then choose ${\mathbf n}_{\alpha}^{1} \in M_{\leq \lambda_{2}}$ such that ${\mathbf n}_{\alpha}^{0} \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf n}_{\alpha}^{1} \in {\mathbf M}_{\rm{ec}}$ (by claim \ref{e37}), without loss of generality $L_{{\mathbf n}_{\alpha}^{1}} \cap L_{{\mathbf m}_{\alpha}} = L_{{\mathbf n}_{\alpha}^{0}}$ so clause $(*)(d)(\beta), (\gamma)$ holds. 
    
    So we have carried the induction. 
    
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[$(*)_{1}$] Let ${\mathbf n} = {\mathbf m}_{\alpha_{*}}$ so ${\mathbf n} \in {\mathbf M}_{\leq\lambda_{2}}$ and ${\mathbf m} = {\mathbf n}_{0} \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf n}.$ 
    \end{itemize}
    
    So clause $\boxplus(a)$ holds. Why ${\mathbf n} \in {\mathbf M}_{\rm{bec}}?$ (i.e.  clause $\boxplus(b)$). As clearly $M_{{\mathbf n}}$ is strongly $(< \lambda^{+})$-directed, by \ref{b47}(5) it  suffices to prove that $M_{{\mathbf n}(\leq t)} \in {\mathbf M}_{\rm{bec}}$ for every $t \in M_{{\mathbf m}}.$ But $M_{{\mathbf n}(\leq t)} \in \{ M_{\alpha}: \alpha < \alpha_{*} \}$ and if $M = M_{{\mathbf m}({\leq t_{\alpha}})}$ then $\rm{rest}(M, {\mathbf n}) \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf m}(\leq t_{\alpha})$ so this follows if we prove clauses $\boxplus(d), (e).$
    
    Why clauses $\boxplus(d), (e)$ holds? So assume $M \in {\mathscr P}^{-}(M_{{\mathbf m}})$ then for some $\alpha = \alpha(M) < \alpha_{*}$ we have $M = M_{\alpha}$ and let $\mathscr{L}_{M} = \rm{cmp}(M, {\mathbf n}_{\alpha}^{1})$ (so $\bigcup \{ L: L \in \mathscr{L}_{M} \} = L_{{\mathbf n}_{\alpha}^{1}}).$ Assume $\rm{rest}({\mathscr{L}}_{M}, M, {\mathbf n}) = {\mathbf n}_{0} \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf n}_{1} \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf n}_{2}$ and we shall prove that ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}_{1}} \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}_{2}},$ this suffices for $\boxplus(e).$ 
    
    Let $\alpha < \alpha_{*}$ be such that $M_{\alpha} = M,$ so clearly. 
    
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[$(*)_{2}$] 
        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[$\bullet_{1}$] $ \rm{rest}(\mathscr{L}_{M}, M, {\mathbf n}) = {\mathbf n}_{\alpha}^{1},$
            
            \item[$\bullet_{2}$] ${\mathbf n}_{\alpha}^{1} = \rm{rest}(M_{\alpha}, {\mathbf m}_{\alpha}),$
            
            \item[$\bullet_{3}$] $\rm{rest}(M_{\alpha}, {\mathbf m}_{\alpha}) \leq_{{\mathbf M}} \rm{rest}(M_{\alpha}, {\mathbf n}),$
            
            \item[$\bullet_{4}$] $\rm{rest}(M_{\alpha}, {\mathbf n}) \leq_{{\mathbf M}} \rm{Rest}(M_{\alpha}, {\mathbf n}) \leq_{{\mathbf M}} \rm{Rest}(M_{\alpha}, {\mathbf n}_{1}) \leq_{{\mathbf M}} \rm{Rest}(M_{\alpha}, {\mathbf n}_{2}).$
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{itemize}
    
    As ${\mathbf n}_{\alpha}^{1} \in {\mathbf M}_{\rm{bec}}$ it follows that $\rm{Rest}(M_{\alpha}, {\mathbf n}_{1}) \lessdot \rm{Rest}(M_{\alpha}, {\mathbf n}_{2}),$ but by \ref{g8}(1),
    
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[$(*)_{3}$]  ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}_{l}} = {\mathbb P}_{\rm{Rest}(M_{\alpha}, {\mathbf n}_{l})}$ for $l = 1, 2.$
    \end{itemize}
    
    So we are done proving $\boxplus(e).$
    
    Now $\boxplus(c)$ is just a choice, so we are left with $\boxplus(f)$ which says ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}_{M}} \lessdot {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf n}}$ but it follows by $(*)_{2}$ and $(*)_{3}.$
    
    \noindent 
    2) We can find ${\mathbf n}^{+}$ such that: 
    
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[$(*)$]
        
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(a)] ${\mathbf n} \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf n}^{+} \in {\mathbf M}_{\leq \lambda_{2}},$ (${\mathbf n}$ is from part (1)),
            
            \item[(b)] if $M_{1}, M_{2} \in {\mathscr P}^{-}(M_{{\mathbf m}})$ and $h$ is an isomorphism from ${\mathbf m} {\restriction} M_{1}$ onto ${\mathbf m} {\restriction} M_{2}$ and $L \in \rm{cmp}(M_{1}, {\mathbf n})$ \underline{then} there is $\langle (L_{i}, {h_{i}}): i < \lambda_{2} \rangle$ such that: 
            \begin{enumerate}
                \item[$(\alpha)$] $L_{i} \in \rm{cmp}(M_{2}, {\mathbf m}),$
                
                \item[$(\beta)$] $h_{i}$ is an  isomorphism from ${\mathbf m} {\restriction} L$ onto ${\mathbf m} {\restriction} L_{i}$ which extends $h {\restriction} (L \cap M_{i}),$
                
                \item[$(\gamma)$] $L_{i} \cap  L_{{\mathbf n}} \subseteq M_{{\mathbf m}}.$
            \end{enumerate}
            
            \item[(c)] if $t \in L_{{\mathbf n}}(t) \setminus L_{{\mathbf n}}$ \underline{then} for some $s \in L_{{\mathbf n}} \setminus M_{{\mathbf m}}$ we have $ {\mathbf n} {\restriction} (t / E_{{\mathbf n}(t), \ast}), {\mathbf n} {\restriction} (s / E_{{\mathbf n}, t})$ are isomorphic, 
            
            \item[(d)] if $s \in L_{{\mathbf n}} \setminus M_{{\mathbf n}}, M_{1} = s / E', M_{2} \in {\mathscr P}^{-}(M_{{\mathbf m}})$ and $h$ is an isomorphism from ${\mathbf m} {\restriction} M_{1}$ onto ${\mathbf m} {\restriction} M_{2},$ \underline{then} there is a sequence $\langle t_{{\varepsilon}}: {\varepsilon} < \lambda_{2} \rangle$ of pairwise non-$E_{{\mathbf n}(t)}''$-equivalent  members of $L_{{\mathbf m}} \setminus M_{{\mathbf m}}$ such that $(t_{\zeta} / E_{{\mathbf m}}') \cap M_{{\mathbf m}} = M_{2}$ and there is an isomorphism from ${\mathbf n} {\restriction} (s / E_{{\mathbf n}}')$ onto ${\mathbf n}^{\dagger} {\restriction} (t_{\zeta} / E_{{\mathbf n}(+)}')$  
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{itemize}
    
    Now we can easily find the isomorphism promised in clause (j). Lastly, clause (k) holds because ${\mathbf n}_{\alpha}^{0} = {\mathbf m} {\restriction} M_{\alpha}$ above. So ${\mathbf n}^{+}$ is as required recalling $t \in L_{{\mathbf n}^{+}} \setminus M_{{\mathbf n}^{+}} \Rightarrow t / E_{{\mathbf n}^{+}}' = \cup \{ L: L \in {\rm cmp}(M_{{\mathbf m}}, {\mathbf m}) \}$ as ${\mathbf m}$ is bounded.  
    
    3) Easy.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- remark-20: body_md -->
\label{g15}
    How does this subsection help \cite{Sh:945}?

    1) Note in the family $\mathbf{R}$ of ${\mathbf r}'$s see Definition \ref{e53} we demand that there is ${\mathbf G}^{+} \subseteq N_{{\mathbf r}} \cap {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ generic over $N$ such that: (so $N \prec ({\mathscr H}(\chi), \in), ({\mathbf n}, \lambda, \cdots) \in N$ and $\mathbf{j}_{N}$ is the Mostowski collapse)
    
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[$(*)$] $\mathbf{j}''_{N}(N)[{\mathbf G}^{+}] = \mathscr{H}(\chi_{{\varepsilon}}), \chi_{{\varepsilon}} = {\rm otp}(N \cap \chi).$ 
    \end{itemize}
    
    You can think of it as: in the preliminary forcing to get Laver diamond, in stage $\lambda_{N} = N \cap \lambda$ we force by $\mathbf{j}_{{\varepsilon}} ({\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}} \cap N).$
    
    2) The present \ref{e70} tells us to use $\Xi_{\nu}^{\bullet}$ (defined in \ref{g5}(4)) that instead of using  $\Xi_{\nu}^{\dagger} = \{ {\mathbf G}: {\mathbf G} \subseteq N_{s} \cap {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}^{\dagger} \ \text{is generic over} \ N \ \text{such that} \ \nu_{\alpha} = \let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3\eta$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}_{\alpha}[{\mathbf G}] \ \text{for} \ \alpha \in M \}$ which gives too may candidates \underline{or} $\Xi_{\bar{\nu}}^{+} = \{ {\mathbf G}: {\mathbf G} \subseteq N \cap {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}} \ \text{is generic over} \ N \ \text{such that} \ \mathbf{j}''(N) [\mathbf{j}_{N}''({\mathbf G})] = {\mathscr H}(\chi_{N}) \ \text{and} \ \nu_{\alpha} = \let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3\eta$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}_{\alpha}[G]\}$ \color{black} which seems too restrictive. 
    
    Enough to use the middle ground $\Xi_{\bar{\nu}}^{\bullet} = \{ {\mathbf G}: {\mathbf G} \subseteq N \cap {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}} \ \text{is generic over} \ N \ \text{and} \ \nu_{\alpha} = \let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3\eta$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}_{\alpha}[{\mathbf G}] \ \text{for} \ \alpha \in M \}.$ 
    
    3) Now the original idea was that ${\mathbf G} \in \Xi_{\bar{\nu}}^{\dagger}$ is enough in \cite{Sh:945} but not so, however ${\mathbf G} \in \Xi_{\bar{\nu}}^{\bullet}$ is sufficient.
    
    4) Also we need that ${\mathbf m}$ is reasonable (see \ref{e36}(3)) so if $M \subseteq M_{{\mathbf m}}$  is cofinal then $\langle \let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3\nu$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}_{\alpha}: \alpha \in M \rangle$ is cofinal for ${\mathbf m}.$  
    
    5) The point is that for $M \nsubseteq M_{{\mathbf m}}$ (or with $M \cap N, M_{{\mathbf m}} \cap N $ the reflection) we need stronger homogeneity of ${\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}},$ which is the aim of \ref{g0}-\ref{g17} relying on \ref{g14}.
<!-- end remark-20 -->
<!-- conclusion-7: body_md -->
\label{g17}
    If ${\mathbf m}_{0} \in {\mathbf M}$ is strongly $\lambda^{+}$-directed, (so bounded) of cardinality $\leq \lambda_{2},$ \underline{then} there is ${\mathbf m}$ such that: 
    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] ${\mathbf m} \in {\mathbf M}$ of cardinality $\lambda_{2},$
        
        \item[(b)] ${\mathbf m}_{0} \leq_{{\mathbf M}} {\mathbf m},$
        
        \item[(c)] ${\mathbf m} \in {\mathbf M}_{\rm{bec}},$
        
        \item[(d)] $(\alpha) \Rightarrow (\beta),$ where: 
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[($\alpha$)]
            
            \begin{enumerate}
                \item[$\bullet_{1}$] ${\mathbf r} \in \mathbf{R}$ and ${\mathbf m}_{{\mathbf r}} = {\mathbf m}$ and $ \langle \eta_{s}: s \in M_{{\mathbf m}} \rangle \in \Xi_{{\mathbf r}}^{+}.$
                
                \item[$\bullet_{2}$] $M' \subseteq M_{{\mathbf m}},$ (in the main case is $M_{{\mathbf m}} \cong (\kappa, <), M_{*}$ a cofinal subset of $M_{{\mathbf m}}$), $M_{*} = M' \cap N_{{\mathbf r}}, M' \in N_{{\mathbf r}},$
                
                \item[$\bullet_{3}$] $h$ is an isomorphism from ${\mathbf m} {\restriction} M_{*}$ onto ${\mathbf m} {\restriction} M_{{\mathbf m}},$
                
                \item[${\bullet_{4}}$] so there is ${\mathbf G}^{+} \subseteq {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}} \cap N_{{\mathbf r}}$ generic over $N_{{\mathbf r}}$ such that $s \in M_{{\mathbf m}} \Rightarrow \eta_{s} = \let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3\eta$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}_{s}[{\mathbf G}^{+}]$ and ${\mathscr H}(\chi_{{\mathbf r}}) = \mathbf{j}_{N}''(N_{{\mathbf r}})[\mathbf{j}_{N}''[{\mathbf G}^{+}]]$ (by the definition of $\mathbf{R}$).
            \end{enumerate}
            
            \item[($\beta$)] there is ${\mathbf G} \subseteq N \cap {\mathbb P}_{{\mathbf m}}$ generic over $N$ such that $s \in M_{*} \Rightarrow \let\theaccent\tilde\skewfactor-
\mathpalette\oalign{$3\eta$\cr\hidewidth
\vbox to.2ex{\hbox{$3\skew\skewfactor\theaccent{}$}\vss}\hidewidth}_{h(s)}[{\mathbf G}] = \eta_{s}.$
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end conclusion-7 -->
